description:
Observed 2026-09-14 by the ub-kp7 (D50) orchestrator's own workspace probe on branch ub-kp7-pre-initialize-gate, which touches nothing below the MCP layer (crates/unblock-storage is byte-unchanged on that branch). Reported rather than swept, the same way ub-q1u was.

SYMPTOM. cargo test --workspace --all-features exited 101 on crates/unblock-storage/tests/write_lock_two_process.rs, cell cross_process_write_lock_prevents_id_collision, at the non-vacuity assertion near :133: "the no-lock control must REPRODUCE the IdCollision (got 0 — the test would be vacuous)". The locked half of the cell passed; the control half, which runs the same two-process race WITHOUT the .write.lock and expects at least one IdCollision, saw zero collisions.

CONDITIONS. The machine was under heavy load at the time (load average around 12 on the probe's finish, with four parallel full workspace builds from Verify-gate worktrees running alongside), so the two child processes of the control race very likely ran serialized by the scheduler and never overlapped, which is exactly the regime in which a race-based non-vacuity control cannot reproduce the race. Re-run three times in isolation on the same tree immediately afterwards: 3 of 3 passed (0.5 to 1.0 s each).

WHY IT MATTERS. The control exists so the locked half cannot pass vacuously, which is right, but a control that depends on two processes actually overlapping is load-sensitive by construction and turns the required test job red for a reason unrelated to the change under test. Sibling of ub-q1u (a load-sensitive libsql stress cell) and of the bench-gate whole-runner degradation class.

REMEDY, to decide rather than assume. Options: make the control's overlap deterministic (a barrier both children pass before their first write, so overlap does not depend on scheduling), retry the control a bounded number of times before declaring vacuity, or move the control under a feature or an ignore that the required job does not run. Do not weaken the locked half.
title: Flaky: write_lock_two_process's no-lock control fails to reproduce the IdCollision under heavy machine load, turning its non-vacuity assertion red

description:
Found by the ub-kp7 (D50) Implement phase on 2026-09-14, in the unblock-cli test harness, and split out because a harness change touches every stdio suite.

WHAT IT IS. McpClient::read_response in crates/unblock-cli/tests/common/mod.rs (the loop that reads the child's stdout until a reply carries the awaited id) checks its 20-second deadline only at the top of each loop iteration, and each iteration blocks in BufReader::read_line. When the child never writes another line, the read blocks forever and the deadline is never consulted, so the test hangs instead of failing with "timed out awaiting response id".

HOW IT WAS FOUND. During the D50 mutation pass, the mutant that makes the gate answer a premature request with an id-less error (id None instead of the frame's own id) produced a reply the harness cannot correlate, the child then parked waiting for more input, and the cell hung for the whole 600-second cargo timeout instead of going red. The three affected cells were restructured onto a sentinel probe to work around it; the harness itself was left as shipped.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every future mutation or regression that turns a correlated reply into an uncorrelated one (or into silence) costs a full timeout instead of a fast red, and a hang on the required test job reads as an infrastructure problem rather than a failing assertion.

REMEDY. Make the deadline bind the blocking read: move stdout reading to a drain thread with a channel and a timed receive (the harness already owns such a thread for capture_stdout), or set a read timeout on the pipe, so read_response fails within its deadline whether or not a line arrives. Keep the NFR-14 framing assertion on every line. Verify with the same id-None mutant of the D50 gate, which must then turn the cells red within the deadline.
title: Bug (test harness): McpClient::read_response blocks past its 20-second deadline when the child never writes a correlatable reply

description:
Filed 2026-08-07 by the ub-gwe design Review gate, which insisted the disclosure be tracked rather than left in a pull-request body. Deliberately NOT bundled into the ub-gwe pull request: the fix lives under .claude, which the run-report gate treats as an always-substantive path, so folding it in would drag a second run-report obligation into a change that is about two prose edits.

WHAT ub-gwe LANDS. A hard rule in CLAUDE.md making the code-graph MCP tools the first move for a structural question (who calls this, is this reachable, which paths do X, what does this depend on), plus a docs/PROCESS.md section 4 paragraph stating that the Understand phase opens at the graph and that an unavailable or stale index is fixed or reported, never silently worked around.

WHY IT IS INERT TODAY FOR EVERY SPAWNED TEAM, measured rather than assumed. All twelve agent definitions under .claude/agents declare an explicit tools allow-list in their frontmatter, and NOT ONE of them lists any tool with the mcp prefix — verified by grepping every definition for that prefix, which returns nothing. The allow-lists are: Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep for cli-developer, code-reviewer, fullstack-developer, git-workflow-manager, mcp-developer, refactoring-specialist and rust-engineer; the same minus Bash for multi-agent-coordinator; Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep plus web tools for project-idea-validator and project-manager; Read/Grep/Glob/Bash plus web tools for research-analyst; and Read/Grep/Glob/Bash for qa-expert. .claude/settings.json grants no MCP permission either: its permissions.allow list carries only path-scoped Edit and Write plus a set of Bash prefixes.

There is a SECOND, independent blocker at the server level. The codebase-memory entry that ub-gwe commits into .mcp.json is a PROJECT-scoped server, and a project-scoped server is inert until the user approves it. The user-level configuration for this project currently carries an EMPTY enabled-servers list and sets no enable-all flag, so a fresh session — and every session on a fresh clone — starts with that server not running even though the entry is committed. Today the graph reaches this repo through a separately-configured user-level server, not through the committed entry. Whoever fixes this must not stop at the agent frontmatter and declare victory.

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly. Every spawned Understand or Verify team lands in the rule's "unavailable" arm and answers structural questions with grep sweeps — which is exactly the behaviour ub-gwe exists to stop. That arm is doing its job (the gap gets reported instead of silently grepped around) but it is a disclosure, not a solution. The only actor that can currently follow the rule is the main-session orchestrator, whose omission opened ub-gwe in the first place.

### Acceptance Criteria
- The code-graph MCP tools are reachable from a spawned agent of at least the Understand and Verify lineups (Plan, rust-engineer, research-analyst, code-reviewer, qa-expert), proven by a live call from inside a spawned agent that returns real graph data — not by reading the configuration and asserting it should work.
- The project-scoped server blocker is settled explicitly: either the committed .mcp.json entry is made to actually start for a session that has not hand-approved it, or the approval step is written down as a required onboarding action, with the reasoning recorded. Committing an entry that never starts is worse than not committing one, because it reads as wired.
- The failure mode is proven, not asserted: with the grant removed, a spawned agent asking a structural question observably lands in the "unavailable" arm and says so, rather than silently grepping.
- The blast radius of the grant is stated: which servers each agent type can reach, and why any server beyond the code graph is or is not included. A blanket grant of every configured MCP server to every agent is a decision, not a default, and must be argued if chosen.
- docs/PROCESS.md section 4 is reconciled with the outcome in the same change if the mechanics it describes change.
title: Chore: spawned agent teams cannot reach the code-graph MCP tools — the ub-gwe Understand rule is unexecutable for every team until they are granted

description:
Raised by the ub-og3 Understand phase, carried unresolved through its Decide phase, and split out by Miguel's ruling at the design Review gate (2026-08-06) so that silence does not make it "out by omission" — which PROCESS section 5 classifies as deferring a gap.

WHAT IT IS, AND WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN. Reasoned from the tokio and rmcp sources, NEVER REPRODUCED. State it as a hypothesis, not a fact, until someone measures it.

The claim: a response frame large enough to span more than one `poll_write` (the tokio stdout path chunks writes) can be left PARTIALLY written if the sending task is dropped mid-write — rmcp drops its send JoinSet on a drain timeout. The write site is `crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs:404`. There is no cap on RESPONSE size: `crates/unblock-mcp/src/options.rs` bounds incoming REQUESTS only (the NFR-18 argument quotas), not what the server writes back.

WHY IT BELONGS NEXT TO ub-og3 BUT IS NOT ub-og3. Both corrupt the JSON-RPC framing channel, so a client hits an unparseable line where a frame belongs. But the failure is a DIFFERENT one: ub-og3 writes a foreign, well-formed line onto the channel; this writes half of a legitimate frame. Different mechanism, different fix, different crate — ub-og3's fix (the exit boundary learns which command owns stdout) does not touch it, and its regression cells would not see it.

FIRST STEP IS MEASUREMENT, NOT A FIX. Construct a response large enough to cross the chunking threshold and force the drain timeout; establish whether truncation actually occurs and at what size. Only then decide the remedy (a response-size cap, moving the write off the cancellable path, or a framing-level guarantee). Note the related ub-nbz already records that writes inside a cancellable future can be lost outright, which may share a root with this.

ALSO UNMEASURED, and to be settled by the same work: Windows. Every measurement in this family is macOS on aarch64; tokio's Windows stdout path splits writes at a UTF-8 boundary and plausibly chunks at a much smaller threshold.
title: Bug (unmeasured): no response-size cap — a large frame can be written to stdout truncated, corrupting the framing channel with a PARTIAL frame

close_reason: PR #442 merged to main on 2026-09-08 (fix(deps): bump h2 to 0.4.19 for RUSTSEC-2026-0258, plus the tracker re-export and the run-report 2026-09-08-h2-advisory-lock-bump). The deny and audit jobs are green on the PR.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand and Decide (2026-09-08, orchestrator, off main at b562570).

graph: unavailable(not applicable) — the task moves a Cargo.lock entry and touches no Rust symbol; the questions are text questions (which lock entry, which dependents, which advisory range), answered by cargo tree and the advisory file. Measured on main: h2 0.4.15 enters through hyper 1.10.1, pulled by reqwest 0.13.4 under axoasset 2.0.1 under axoupdater 0.10.0 (the unblock-cli self-update path) and by wiremock 0.6.5 (unblock-cli dev-dependency). RUSTSEC-2026-0258 is patched at h2 0.4.16, semver-compatible, so a lock-only bump satisfies both the deny and the audit job. No manifest, contract, schema or decision-id movement; no run-report obligation unless the run-report gate classifies the lock diff as substantive, in which case Track writes one.

Decide: proportionality applies (docs/PROCESS.md section 4). One implementer on opus at maximum effort in an isolated worktree runs the bump and the local proofs (cargo deny check, cargo audit where installed, cargo build and the unblock-cli tests under --locked, the no-network confinement test if runnable locally), then one Verify lens re-derives the lock diff and the advisory clearance, then Track lands the tracker re-export on the same branch and Claude opens the PR. Branch ub-5xl-h2-rustsec-2026-0258. PR #441 (ub-wvh) is rebased onto main after this lands, not onto this branch.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Implement summary (2026-09-08, one rust-engineer on opus at maximum effort, isolated worktree). Branch ub-5xl-h2-rustsec-2026-0258 carries one commit, 01eb3d0, fix(deps): bump h2 to 0.4.19 for RUSTSEC-2026-0258, on top of main b562570. Cargo.lock is the only file touched (12 insertions, 12 deletions). Not pushed.

What moved. h2 0.4.15 to 0.4.19, the version cargo update -p h2 resolves (the advisory's own prescribed remedy; 0.4.16 is only its floor, and the orchestrator accepts 0.4.19 so the lock stays reproducible from that command rather than from a --precise pin three patches behind). Ten windows-sys dependency edges re-pointed from 0.61.2 to 0.60.2 or 0.52.0 because those crates declare range requirements and the resolver re-unifies a range onto a version already in the graph; the three windows-sys versions present before are all present after, nothing was added or removed, and the package set stays at 385 entries. The orchestrator accepts the resolver's diff over a hand-built h2-only lock, which cargo would accept but no command reproduces.

Proofs, all in the worktree. Before the bump cargo audit and cargo deny check both fail on RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (the red baseline). After it: cargo audit exit 0 over 385 dependencies; cargo deny check exit 0 on all four checks, with the twenty-three pre-existing duplicate warnings unchanged; cargo build --workspace --locked exit 0; cargo test -p unblock-cli --locked 218 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, including the five wiremock-backed update_verify tests that drive the real unblock update HTTP path; cargo xtask no-network exit 0; the four feature-matrix steps as ci.yml runs them, exit 0 with reqwest, hyper, axoupdater, rustls and h2 absent from the no-default-features tree and axoupdater present under self-update; cargo xtask check-layering and cargo fmt --check exit 0. Not run, left to CI: clippy, the workspace test, snapshots, storage testkit, stress, bench, scale, rate-limit, doc-lint and its scripts, run-report-gate.

Finding worth recording: the shipped binary never linked the vulnerable code. On runtime edges hyper resolves without its optional h2 feature, so cargo build --workspace compiles no h2 and cargo tree with normal edges never shows it, even with self-update on; h2 is compiled only through wiremock, a dev-dependency, which enables hyper's http2. cargo-deny and cargo-audit read the lockfile rather than the unit graph, so the gates were red regardless and the bump remains the correct fix. User-facing severity was nil; the impact was on CI.

Verify follows with one lens (proportionality: a lock-only bump), then Track.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Verify gate (2026-09-08, one code-reviewer lens on opus at maximum effort, own worktree detached at 01eb3d0; proportionality for a lock-only bump). Tree: PASS. Commit message: three sentences to repair, amended by the orchestrator without touching the tree.

Tree evidence, all re-derived rather than read off the implementer. The lock diff parsed with tomllib and cargo metadata on both trees: exactly one (name, version) entry changes, h2 0.4.15 to 0.4.19, 385 packages on both sides, no checksum change on any shared entry, windows-sys versions {0.52.0, 0.60.2, 0.61.2} and windows-targets {0.52.6, 0.53.5} present on both sides, and exactly ten packages change one windows-sys edge each, every one landing on the lowest already-activated version its declared range admits. Strongest proof: on a pristine copy of main, cargo update -p h2 reproduces the committed lock byte for byte, so nothing was hand-edited and no narrower command avoids the edge movements. cargo audit and cargo deny check are red on main (the counterfactual) and green at the commit. cargo build --workspace --locked, cargo test -p unblock-cli --locked (218 passed), cargo test --workspace --locked (1714 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored), cargo xtask no-network, the four feature-matrix steps as ci.yml writes them, and cargo fmt --check are all green. The build emits zero h2 compile units; hyper resolves with client, default and http1 on runtime edges, and the http2 feature is requested by wiremock alone, so the commit message's account of the shipped binary never linking h2 is correct.

Message repairs. The claim that the advisory itself names cargo update -p h2 as the remedy was false (the advisory file and cargo-audit say only "upgrade to >= 0.4.16"; the command appears in cargo-deny's rendering), so the sentence now attributes reproducibility to the command without attributing the command to the advisory. The quantifier "every range requirement" over a list that omitted quinn-udp and rustix 0.38.44 (range requirements that did not move because they already sat on an activated version) is now scoped to the edges that moved, and the count word in front of that list is gone. One colon-hinged clause is split into two sentences per STYLE.md.

Advisories carried into the message and the PR body: the change makes nine more crate versions reachable in cargo-deny's default graph (windows-targets 0.53.5 and its eight arch crates, because windows-sys 0.60.2 was reachable on main only through quinn-udp), raising the duplicate-version warnings from fourteen to twenty-three; the gate stays green because deny.toml warns rather than denies on multiple versions, and the tightening deny.toml announces later would then name this commit. No CI job compiles the re-pointed Windows edges, since every job runs on ubuntu-latest; the release pipeline's x86_64-pc-windows-msvc build is their first real compile, and cargo check for that target after rustup target add would close the gap before a release.

Gate classification for Track: scripts/knowledge/run-report-gate.sh main reports "pure manifest diff — pass", exit 0, so no wiki run-report is owed for this PR; the tracker re-export lands as a second commit, and its comments carry no session-local codes, which keeps the classification.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text: Track result (2026-09-08). Branch ub-5xl-h2-rustsec-2026-0258 carries e524335 (the lock bump, message amended after Verify with the tree unchanged), 6b71306 (the tracker re-export) and 9ed07fd (the wiki run-report 2026-09-08-h2-advisory-lock-bump and its index line). description:
Found 2026-09-08 by the CI run of PR #441 (ub-wvh), whose diff touches no Cargo manifest or lock. The deny job (cargo-deny advisories) and the audit job (cargo-audit) both fail on RUSTSEC-2026-0258, published 2026-08-17: the h2 crate accepted and queued empty HTTP/2 DATA frames without limit, so an undrained stream could grow memory without bound or panic on a length overflow. Low severity per the advisory. Patched in h2 0.4.16. The last CI run on main (2026-08-07) predates the advisory and passed; any PR opened now fails both jobs until the lock moves.

Where it enters the graph (cargo tree -i h2 on main b562570): h2 0.4.15 <- hyper 1.10.1 <- hyper-rustls 0.27.9 / hyper-util 0.1.20 <- reqwest 0.13.4 <- axoasset 2.0.1 <- axoupdater 0.10.0 <- unblock-cli (the explicit `unblock update` path, D13/NFR-6: the only network path), and separately <- wiremock 0.6.5 (dev-dependency of unblock-cli). No normal command path links h2 at runtime beyond the self-update command.

Expected fix: a Cargo.lock-only bump (cargo update -p h2, semver-compatible within 0.4), no manifest change, no contract movement, no decision id. Verify the feature-matrix and no-network jobs (NFR-17 confinement) stay green, since the crate sits under the self-update feature. Patch-eligible for v1.0.1.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Cargo.lock carries h2 >= 0.4.16 and nothing else moves unless cargo requires it; the diff names every crate that moved.
- The deny and audit jobs are green on the PR and on main after merge.
- The feature-matrix, no-network and test jobs stay green.
- The commit is Conventional (chore(deps) or fix(deps)) and names the advisory id.
title: Bug: RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (h2 0.4.15 unbounded empty DATA frames) reddens the required deny and audit jobs on every PR; bump the lock to h2 >= 0.4.16

description:
Found 2026-08-05 by the ub-cnv Understand phase. Filed by the orchestrator so a known residual is tracked rather than left implicit: Miguel scoped ub-cnv to the un-decodable-id class only, so this neighbouring class is deliberately NOT closed there and must not be claimed closed by it.

OBSERVATION. A frame carrying a duplicated `method` member, or a duplicated `jsonrpc` member, fails the typed parse and is answered with the out-of-band parse error -32700 — with the id OMITTED, unconditionally, even when the raw bytes carry a perfectly readable one (crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs:213-225 passes None as the id).

WHY THAT IS NOT HARMLESS. rmcp's own CLIENT drops an error response that has no id (rmcp src/service.rs:1030-1036), and its request future has no timeout at all — `Peer::send_request` uses `no_options` (:442-447) so `await_response` is an untimed await (:345). So the pending request is never resolved and the caller waits forever, exactly as in the ub-cnv silent class. The only difference is that a byte a human can see was written to the connection, which is why ub-cnv's re-scoped acceptance criterion (no frame that rmcp itself would answer may go unanswered) is satisfied by these frames on its letter while the caller is still stuck.

THE TENSION TO RESOLVE, and it is why this is not a one-line change. JSON-RPC 2.0 says that when there was an error detecting the id, the response id MUST be Null. Our shipped assertion pins the opposite — that the error reply OMITS the id rather than sending a null one (wire.rs:567-570) — following the newer MCP guidance rmcp itself cites (rmcp src/model.rs:464-466). Changing what the transport writes also breaks the byte-identity contract with rmcp's own transport that the CD-7 differential harness enforces (wire.rs:524, assertions :544-552), which exists to catch a framing divergence on a dependency bump. So this is a contract question, not a patch.

DEPENDS ON ub-cnv landing first: that change already establishes both the id-recovery machinery and the re-specified byte-identity contract, and doing this one first would duplicate both.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Decided explicitly, with the JSON-RPC MUST and the MCP guidance both quoted: does the parse-error reply carry a recovered id, a null id, or no id — and if the answer differs by case, the cases are enumerated.
- Whatever ships, a client that sent a request with a duplicated method or jsonrpc member no longer waits forever, or the residual is stated in the spine and the decision row as deliberately accepted with its reason.
- The byte-identity contract with rmcp's transport is reconciled, not merely re-blessed: it must still catch a framing divergence introduced by an rmcp version bump.
- Regression coverage at the raw-bytes wire level, each cell naming the mutant it kills.
title: Bug: the transport's -32700 reply omits a readable request id, so a duplicated method/jsonrpc frame leaves an rmcp client pending forever

description:
Observed 2026-09-21 while running the Understand phase of ub-w3a, off main at 1ff74f2.

SYMPTOM. The codebase-memory graph index returns results whose `name` field does not belong to the
node the rest of the row describes.

  search_graph(name_pattern="LibsqlStorage") returned exactly one hit, and it was
  crates/unblock-model/src/id.rs ParsedId::is_child_of — a method in a different crate with no relation
  to the name searched for. Zero of the real LibsqlStorage nodes came back.

  search_graph(qn_pattern="unblock-storage.src.libsql") returned 299 correct nodes, but their `name`
  fields carry unrelated strings, several of them markdown section headings. Examples from that one
  page of results: the module crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/ids.rs came back named
  "3. Milestone M1 — Engine + core domain"; the function escape_like_pattern came back named
  "4. Milestone M2 — MCP surface (primary)"; the test comments_column_order_golden came back named
  "GLOSSARY_NONE"; the variable MIGRATIONS came back named "CONTRACT_RE".

READING. The qualified_name, file_path, signature, docstring and metric fields all look correct and
self-consistent. Only `name` is wrong, and the wrong values look like names harvested from documents
in the same repository. That points at the name column being populated from a separately ordered list
and zipped onto code nodes out of order, rather than at a parsing failure.

The index is not stale. index_status reports the project at head_sha 1ff74f2, which is current main,
with 7597 nodes and 36026 edges.

IMPACT. Every discovery path that starts from a symbol name is unusable, and it fails misleadingly
rather than emptily. A name search returns a confident single hit pointing at the wrong file. Anything
downstream that reads the name field — an agent summarising results, a human scanning them — is being
handed wrong symbol names attached to right locations. The project process makes the graph the
mandatory first stop for structural questions, so this silently degrades the first move of every task.

WORKAROUND IN USE. Query by qualified-name prefix and read the qualified_name field, ignoring `name`;
fall back to direct file reads for symbol lookup. That is what ub-w3a is doing.

NEXT STEP. Reproduce against a rebuilt index to tell a persistent indexer bug from a corrupted build of
this particular index. If a rebuild fixes it, the question becomes what made this build wrong and
whether it can recur silently.
title: Bug: the codebase-memory graph index returns a misaligned name column, so symbol-name lookups point at the wrong code

description:
Found at the ub-b1a Verify gate (2026-09-10) and split out so it is tracked rather than left to recur.

WHAT HAPPENED. The D49 spec commit (docs/PRD.md row D49, the unblock-mcp and unblock-error crate-plan rows, the T3.12 block) cited about fifteen file:line anchors into crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs and crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/bulk_markdown.rs. The implementation commit that followed added about 127 lines to error.rs, so every anchor below the insertion point pointed at the wrong line on the PR head (for example "the D38 doc comment at error.rs:62" resolved to a D49 doc line; the comment had moved to :189). cargo xtask doc-lint exited 0 over all of it: no class checks that a cited line carries what the sentence claims. The Verify gate caught it only because three lenses re-derived every anchor by hand (128, 34 and 24 anchors respectively), and the repair had to renumber them all.

WHY IT MATTERS. The repo's hierarchy (PRD > spine > crate plans) is enforced by prose that anchors claims on lines; a stale anchor sends the next implementer into the wrong crate to find nothing (the exact failure D48 clause 6(ii) records for an earlier draft). Every spec-first change that lands code AFTER its spec commit re-creates the condition, and the repair is manual each time.

DECIDE FIRST. Options: (a) a doc-lint class that resolves every `path:line` or `path:start-end` anchor in the 19-file corpus and checks the cited line(s) contain a token the sentence names (needs a convention for what token, e.g. a backticked identifier in the same sentence); (b) a convention that normative docs anchor on IDENTIFIERS (fn names, const names, row ids) and never on bare line numbers for files the same change edits, with line numbers reserved for external sources (rmcp) pinned at a version; (c) accept the manual sweep as a Verify-gate duty and write it into PROCESS section 5. Each has a cost: (a) is real xtask code and a convention; (b) changes how every future row is written; (c) is the status quo that just cost a gate round.

RELATION. The k6 glossary lint and the D-range knobs show the repo prefers executable checks over remembered duties (feedback: derived counts die in prose plans). This is the same class one level down.
title: Finding: file:line anchors in normative docs rot silently when the anchored code moves; no lint class catches it

description:
Surfaced 2026-09-21 by the ub-w3a research spike. The scope below is the orchestrator's own reading of
our code, not a lens report, and it deliberately narrows a broader claim that did not survive checking.

UPSTREAM. libsql issue #2271, opened 2026-08-13, still open with no maintainer reply, reports that the
SQLite core bundled in libsql-ffi predates the upstream write-ahead-log reset fix that landed in SQLite
3.51.3. The race is the long-standing one where a write transaction racing a checkpoint during a
write-ahead-log reset leaves the checkpointer confused about which pages were copied, so committed
writes are silently lost or the file corrupts. The reporter names the triggering topology precisely: a
separate process checkpointing while other connections write, which is the shape of running an external
replication or backup tool against the database.

The version premise holds for us. libsql-ffi 0.9.30 bundles SQLITE_VERSION "3.45.1", confirmed at
bundled/bindings/bindgen.rs:27 and bundled/src/sqlite3.c. No libsql release carries the fix.

WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED, AND WHY. unblock's own checkpoints cannot produce the race.

  Session::acquire (crates/unblock-engine/src/session/write.rs:123) takes the in-process write permit
  and then the cross-process advisory lock, and holds the returned guard across the whole mutation.

  The passive checkpoint fires inside with_immediate_tx (crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/mod.rs:529)
  after the commit and before that guard drops. It therefore runs while the exclusive advisory lock is
  held, so no other unblock process can be inside a write transaction at that moment.

  wal_autocheckpoint is set to zero, so no implicit checkpoint fires on any other connection. Every
  checkpoint we take is explicit.

  The migrate path's TRUNCATE checkpoint (crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/migrations.rs:283) runs
  under the same advisory lock, taken explicitly with a zero timeout.

An earlier framing of this finding called it a live data-loss exposure on the shipped 1.0.0. That
framing is wrong and should not be repeated.

WHAT IS AFFECTED. The advisory lock is advisory. A FOREIGN process that checkpoints our write-ahead log
reproduces the reported topology exactly, and nothing in unblock prevents it. The realistic cases are a
replication or backup tool pointed at the workspace, a snapshotting agent, or a person running the
sqlite3 command-line against .unblock/unblock.db while a session is writing.

SCOPE OF THE ASK. Documentation, not code. Two things worth deciding:

  Whether the workspace documentation should carry a stated limitation that no external tool may
  checkpoint the database file while unblock is running, and name the bundled core version as the
  reason so the note can be retired when a libsql release rebases past 3.51.3.

  Whether the health surface should notice the case at all. A foreign checkpoint is observable after
  the fact through write-ahead-log state, so this may be a diagnostic rather than a prose warning. That
  is a design question, not an obvious yes.

NOT A BLOCKER for the v1.3 direction either way, since the same bundled core ships today.
title: Known limitation: a foreign process checkpointing our WAL can silently lose writes on the bundled SQLite 3.45.1

description:
Raised 2026-08-07 by the ub-gwe Verify gate and sharpened while filing: the gate's original wording said AGENTS.md under-reports the new server, which is true but understates the structural reason.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THE CASE, verified at source. AGENTS.md is 129 lines and ALL of them sit between a BEGIN-unblock and an END-unblock marker pair on lines 1 and 129 — there is not one line outside the generated block. The file is machine-written by the separate `unblock agents` command from the server's own capabilities resource, and it describes the unblock tracker exclusively: how to start it, its contract id, its discovery resources, and a table of its tools and their full parameter surfaces. So it is not merely missing a section about the code-graph server; it has no place to PUT one that a regeneration would not overwrite.

The claim that this contradicts CLAUDE.md does NOT hold, and is recorded here so nobody re-raises it: the CLAUDE.md document-map row that names .mcp.json together with AGENTS.md is itself scoped to the unblock tracker by its own row heading. It is accurate as written.

THE REAL GAP. ub-gwe commits a SECOND MCP server into .mcp.json — a code graph — and makes its use a hard rule for structural questions. After that change, the repository contains no agent-facing description of that server anywhere: not what it is, not what its tools are called, not how to install the binary it runs (which lives outside this public repository), not how to tell whether its index is fresh. A reader who clones this repo gets an entry in .mcp.json that names a command they do not have, and a rule telling them to use it. The hardening applied to the process guide in ub-gwe names the two tool verbs, which is the minimum; it is deliberately not a description of the server.

RELATED, and probably one piece of work with them: issue ub-4ne, which records that the committed entry is project-scoped and therefore inert until approved, and that no spawned agent can reach the tools at all.

### Acceptance Criteria
- A decision is recorded on WHERE a non-unblock MCP server is described for agents, given that AGENTS.md is a generated single-server artifact: candidates are a .knowledge/wiki/topics/ runbook, a section of README, or an out-of-block region of AGENTS.md that the generator provably preserves. If an out-of-block region is chosen, the generator's preservation of it is proven by running the command and diffing, not assumed.
- Whatever is chosen names, at minimum: what the server is, how to obtain and run the binary, its indexing and status tool verbs, and how a reader tells whether the index matches the commit they are working on.
- The choice is reconciled with the process guide's section 4 paragraph so there is one description and one pointer to it, not two descriptions that can drift apart.
- Explicit non-goal, recorded rather than assumed: this does NOT make the code graph a normative document. It holds no rank in the PRD over spine over crate-plans hierarchy, and nothing normative may originate in whatever page ends up describing it.
title: Docs: the repo describes no MCP server other than unblock — AGENTS.md is a fully generated unblock-only block, so the second server lands undocumented

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Scope correction (2026-09-22), superseding one paragraph of this task's description.

The description says this cascade must NOT decide the offline clause, and must mark it pending because
no cache decision existed. Miguel has since decided it: unblock does NOT support offline. There is local
mode or online mode and nothing else. No cache is built, and the three cache options are closed.

So this cascade LANDS the offline clause as decided instead of marking it pending. The roadmap's
shared-state clause stating that reads stay local and offline means read-only is SUPERSEDED outright,
because it belongs to the embedded-replica design this spike ruled out. Remote mode is online; when the
network is unavailable the tool does not work, reads included.

Everything else in the description stands unchanged, including the decision-id range bump list.
Rationale and the stated consequence are on ub-w3a.

description:
Spec-first cascade landing Miguel's 2026-09-22 product decision from the ub-w3a spike. Miguel chose
this to land NOW as its own cascade rather than waiting for the v1.3 lock, so the decision does not age
inside an issue comment while the documents say something else.

=== THE DECISION TO RECORD ===

unblock has TWO user-facing modes, and the product must say so plainly.

  LOCAL MODE. One SQLite file. This is what unblock does today. A solo developer, or a team that does
  not need to share yet, stays here: no network, no server, no account.

  REMOTE MODE. One shared database, every developer connected to the same one. Two server options,
  and the application code does not distinguish between them. Only the URL and the token differ.
  Either a private sqld the team runs, or Turso Cloud.

SQLD IS PRESENTED AS A PEER OF TURSO CLOUD, CARRYING A DATED STATUS NOTE (Miguel's choice, 2026-09-22,
from three options: peers with a note, peers unqualified, or Cloud-first with sqld as advanced). The
note states that the vendor has placed the server in deep maintenance and no longer runs it in
production, that the client-facing port has no transport encryption so a proxy must terminate it, and
that authentication must be configured explicitly because it fails OPEN when it is not. The note
carries its date and its source so it can be retired if the situation changes, rather than becoming
permanent prose nobody dares touch.

=== WHAT THE EVIDENCE BEHIND THIS IS ===

All of it is measured and recorded in this issue's comment thread, not inferred. The same client crate
turso_serverless 0.1.3, which audits clean, was run against a local libsql-server in Docker and against
a real Turso Cloud database. Both passed the same three probes: a remote write read back by an
independent client with no local file, identifier allocation serialized correctly under concurrency,
and a row plus its audit event committing atomically or rolling back together. The probes differed only
in URL and token.

=== SCOPE OF THE CASCADE ===

MINT a new decision id in the product requirements document section 4. It is a NEW id rather than an
amendment because the motivation is separate from any shipped row: it decides the product's mode shape
and its supported servers. It SUPERSEDES the two-axis framing that the roadmap's shared-state section
currently poses, where the axes were where the primary lives and which sync mechanism carries it. Both
reciprocal cross-references are required, never a silent overwrite.

REWRITE the roadmap's shared-state section. The hosting axis becomes a deployment choice rather than an
architecture one. The mechanism becomes SQL over HTTP through turso_serverless, replacing embedded
replicas, and the reason embedded replicas are out is recorded: their only Rust client fails our own
required advisory job with five vulnerabilities we cannot bump past.

RESOLVE ub-jv2 in the same movement. The storage crate's cargo feature is named after the wrong libsql
constructor, and the correct naming falls out of this decision because remote mode no longer uses any
of those three libsql shapes.

THE D-RANGE BUMP, which is the part that rots if it is done by feel. Minting an id moves the live range
from D1..D50 to D1..D51 at every site docs/PROCESS.md section 3 names, in the SPEC commit, as a list
that carries no count. The three prose sites are CLAUDE.md's document map at line 17, the continuous
integration document's class-(a) statement at line 65, and the xtask doc-lint tokenizer comment at line
455. The script knobs are RANGE_RE in scripts/checks/d44-create-deps-claims.sh, and RANGE_RE together
with RANGE_ALT_RE in d46-schema-migration-claims.sh, d47-envelope-id-claims.sh,
d48-stdout-channel-claims.sh, d49-startup-failure-render-claims.sh, d50-pre-handshake-gate-claims.sh and
ub-lp9.25-dangling-blocker-claims.sh. The sibling prose standing above those knobs, the lines quoting
both spellings and the next-id sentences, bumps with them. Every one of those scripts is a step of the
required doc-lint job, so a bump that stops at the prose turns required steps red for reasons unrelated
to their own decisions.

THE DECISION-CHANGE CHECKLIST from docs/PROCESS.md section 3 applies in one commit: the decision row and
any superseded sibling, the product requirements document's dependent sections, the roadmap, the
readme, the continuous integration document, the implementation plan, the owning crate plan, and the
design spine. It is not done until a search for the old framing returns zero live hits, and that search
must be executable rather than a claim in prose.

=== WHAT THIS CASCADE MUST NOT DECIDE, BECAUSE IT IS STILL OPEN ===

The offline clause. The roadmap currently states that reads stay local and that offline means
read-only. Remote mode as measured has no offline at all, not even reads. Miguel has said offline
read-only matters to him and asked whether a local cache can serve it. Three ways to hold that cache
were put to him and none is chosen yet: the turso crate's sync used pull-only, which is vendor
supported but adds a second SQL engine to the binary and needs a server serving the sync endpoint; the
libsql embedded replica, which is out on the advisory finding; or a mirror of our own fed by the
append-only events table, which adds no engine and works against any server but makes the refresh logic
ours. A design question sits under all three, namely whether the cache is the primary read path, which
is fast but can lag, or only a fallback used when the network is down, which keeps every developer
seeing the same instant.

So this cascade lands the mode shape and the server options, and leaves the offline clause explicitly
marked as pending a separate decision. Landing a rewritten offline clause without that decision would
be inventing product behaviour.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

The decision row exists with its reciprocal cross-references. The roadmap section reads correctly for
someone who has not read this issue. The status note on sqld carries a date and a source. The live
range is consistent at every site named above, proven by the required doc-lint job passing rather than
by assertion. A search for the superseded two-axis framing returns zero live hits, proven by a command.
ub-jv2 is resolved. The offline clause is visibly marked pending rather than silently left stale. Both
gates pass before any commit, per the usual discipline.
title: Spec-first cascade: record the two product modes (local SQLite / remote shared) and the two supported remote servers

close_reason: Merged to main via PR 443 (2026-09-11, rebase-merge, tip b7940bb) as decision D49. Gate script d49-startup-failure-render-claims.sh wired as a required doc-lint step. Residuals stay open in ub-kp7, ub-o8s, ub-wx3 and ub-8c4. Both gates were closed by Miguel-ruled escalation after two failed rounds each; recorded as such in the comment thread and the PR body.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Orchestrator orientation (2026-09-09), off main at 4f0ab59, binary target/debug/unblock (crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs and crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs unchanged since 2026-08-07, so the binary is current for this path). graph: used (codebase-memory index at 4f0ab59; it confirmed the single render chain run_with -> into_exit -> to_structured -> StructuredError::from_code and the single caller of run_mcp_server, commands/mcp.rs::run).

MEASURED with a raw stdio probe, one spawn per case, first frame on stdin, streams captured separately. Script kept in the session scratchpad, out of the repo. Every case: stdout 0 bytes, exit 1, the full StructuredError document on stderr, message roughly one for one with the input.

1. notifications/cancelled first (the issue's reproduction): stderr 490 bytes, message 292 bytes, verbatim as the issue quotes it.
2. tools/list request first: the Debug rendering of the TYPED variant (ListToolsRequest ... params: None), 289 bytes. Bounded, because that variant carries no client payload.
3. tools/call request first with a 20,000-byte string inside params.arguments: message 20,369 bytes. So a TYPED request leaks too, whenever its params carry a JSON value.
4. custom request with a 100,000-byte STRING id: message 100,263 bytes. The envelope id is a second attacker-controlled field; the issue text names only method and params.
5. notification with a 100,000-byte method: 100,269 bytes. 5,000,000-byte method: 5,000,269 bytes. Matches the 2026-08-07 measurement.
6. notification with a 20,000-byte nested params value: 20,335 bytes.
7. RESPONSE frame first (id 1, a 20,000-byte result): 20,233 bytes. ERROR frame first (a 20,000-byte error.message): 20,236 bytes. Both JsonRpcMessage shapes reach the same rmcp arm, so all FOUR shapes leak, not only Request and Notification.
8. method and params carrying ESC and BEL bytes plus non-ASCII: the bytes arrive already escaped as \u{1b} and \u{7} because Rust's Debug of a String escapes control characters itself, and sanitize_message then finds nothing to change. Control-character injection is closed twice over; only length and structure are open, as the issue says.

WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS ABOUT THE ORIGIN. rmcp 1.7.0 service/server.rs:52-83 defines ServerInitializeError as #[non_exhaustive]. Its ExpectedInitializeRequest(Option<ClientJsonRpcMessage>) variant is the only one rmcp constructs with the client's frame inside (server.rs:193 for any non-Request, :201 for a non-initialize Request), and its Display is the whole frame's Debug. One more variant carries a client-supplied value: UnsupportedProtocolVersion(ProtocolVersion) at :233, raised when the client's protocol_version does not compare with the server's; ProtocolVersion is a Cow<str> newtype, so its length bound and the reachability of that arm are open questions for the Understand phase. ConnectionClosed carries only rmcp's own static context string, TransportError carries an I/O error, Cancelled carries nothing.

WHAT A NAIVE CLIP WOULD DO. The D43 bound (crates/unblock-error/src/sanitize.rs, MAX_ECHOED_BYTES = 128) applied to the rendered message would cut it at "...but received: Some(Notification(JsonRpcNotification { jsonrpc: JsonRpcVersion2_0, notification: Custo" and the operator would learn nothing about the frame. The structural prefix rmcp writes is already about 150 bytes before the first client byte appears. So the issue's first option (a length cap alone) and its second (a structural summary: frame kind, method, id, never params) are not interchangeable; the summary can clip its client-supplied members with the same D43 helper and stay readable.

WHAT NO TEST PINS. No test, snapshot, or doc quotes the "expect initialized request" text: the only pinned spelling is the prefix "mcp server error: failed to start the MCP server" (crates/unblock-cli/tests/mcp_stdout_channel.rs:262, a constant used to describe the OLD stdout blob) and the D38 verbatim "failed to start the MCP server: Cancelled" in a doc comment (crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs:62). The D48 clause (3) byte-equality cell compares the same CliError rendered under two classifications, so it is content-agnostic and a message change cannot contradict it.

DECISION IDENTITY, pre-decided upstream: PRD D48 clause 6(ii) ends "the repair belongs at the message's ORIGIN, in another crate and under its own decision (Miguel, 2026-08-07)". So this work mints a new D-id, with the D-range bump at every site PROCESS section 3 lists (CLAUDE.md document map, ci-cd section 2.1(a), the xtask doc_lint tokenizer comment, and the RANGE_RE / RANGE_ALT_RE knobs of the five shipped gate scripts, all currently at D1..D48), plus reciprocal cross-references on D47 clause 8(iii) and D48 clause 6(ii), the roadmap bullet that says ub-b1a "stays OPEN", and docs/roadmap.html, which sits outside the doc-lint corpus.

Understand phase is briefed on: every consumer of McpServerError's Display (the json/robot arm, the D38 emit_diagnostic line, the tracing debug route); whether the stderr diagnostic text is a D35-stable surface; whether ProtocolVersion is bounded and its arm reachable; which rmcp accessors can build a summary without reaching into params; and the full spec cascade with file:line.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
UNDERSTAND phase closed (2026-09-09), main at 4f0ab59. Three lenses (architecture, Rust + rmcp mechanics, docs and cascade) ran in parallel in isolated worktrees, a coordinator consolidated them, and the orchestrator re-verified every claim below against source before writing this. graph: used.

THE CHAIN, one interpolation. rmcp 1.7.0 service/server.rs:53-54 renders the whole client frame with Debug inside ServerInitializeError::ExpectedInitializeRequest; crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs:35 carries it through the Transport variant's snafu display; crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:80 wraps it once more, :139 calls to_string() exactly once, :145 sanitizes control characters and nothing else. A fix at error.rs:35 covers every consumer at once, including the plain-format human line and the D38 diagnostic line.

WHAT IS UNBOUNDED. Every one of the four JSON-RPC frame shapes (Request, Notification, Response, Error). The client-supplied fields Debug prints are the envelope id when it is a string, the method, params, result, and error.message. Measured one for one, no cap (orientation comment above). Control characters are already escaped by Rust's Debug of String before sanitize_message runs.

WHAT IS NOT A ROUTE. Of the eight ServerInitializeError variants, exactly one echoes client bytes on the shipped path. UnsupportedProtocolVersion (server.rs:233) carries a client value but cannot fire, because ProtocolVersion derives PartialOrd over a Cow<str> (rmcp model.rs:138-140) whose ordering is total, so partial_cmp never returns None; our VersionClampingTransport (crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:504) also rewrites unknown versions first. UnexpectedInitializeResponse and InitializeFailed carry our own service's values. ExpectedInitializedNotification is deprecated and never constructed; naming it in a match arm would need an allow(deprecated), so a wildcard arm is the right shape.

FIX PLACEMENT, no fork. PRD D48 clause 6(ii) rules the repair belongs at the origin under its own decision. unblock-error is already a dependency of unblock-mcp (crates/unblock-mcp/Cargo.toml:28), so the D43 clip helper (crates/unblock-error/src/sanitize.rs:48-57, MAX_ECHOED_BYTES 128, a SOFT bound because sanitization can expand a control character about six times afterwards) is reachable with no layering change. CONTRACT_HASH digests only (capabilities(), schema_bundle()) (crates/unblock-mcp/src/options.rs:129), so the message text is not a D35 surface and unblock.mcp.v1.9 stands. A snafu display attribute calling a helper function has in-repo precedent (crates/unblock-sync/src/error.rs:26).

WHY A NAIVE CLIP IS A NON-FIX. rmcp's structural prefix ("expect initialized request, but received: Some(Notification(JsonRpcNotification { jsonrpc: ..., notification: Custo") is longer than 128 bytes on its own, so clipping the rendered string leaves the operator with nothing about the frame, while the multi-megabyte string is still built in memory before the cut. A structural summary needs a hand-written match: ClientRequest has a method() accessor (rmcp model.rs:3291-3313); ClientNotification has none (five variants at :3316-3323); NumberOrString implements Display (:224-231) but its String arm needs its own clip.

WHAT NO TEST PINS. Nothing asserts the message text. The cell that provokes the error (crates/unblock-cli/tests/mcp_lifecycle.rs:417) asserts only code and retryable (:455-462). The only live spellings are the D38 doc comment "failed to start the MCP server: Cancelled" (error.rs:62), which must stay byte-identical, and a harness fixture prefix (tests/mcp_stdout_channel.rs:262).

ADJACENT SINKS, found and scoped. (1) rmcp Debug-dumps every POST-handshake frame under tracing (rmcp service.rs:985 info for notifications, :942 debug for requests), and our filter directive at crates/unblock-cli/src/logging.rs:39 is a global floor, so a single -v already prints unbounded client bytes to stderr per frame. Different origin, separate defect. (2) crates/unblock-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:245-246 Debug-renders the whole error through tracing's ? sigil, but only on the two demoted routes (cancellation, pre-initialize disconnect), so it cannot fire for this variant today. (3) crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs:189-190 reads a line with deliberately no length bound, exactly as rmcp; a cap there changes what the server accepts, not what it prints. (4) crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/bulk_markdown.rs:120-129 carries a second, undocumented echo bound (80 chars) and a hard-coded copy of the truncation marker.

DOC CASCADE for the new decision. Sites that assert this issue is OPEN and go false: docs/PRD.md:130 (D47 clause 8(iii)), docs/PRD.md:131 (D48 clause 6(ii)), docs/plans/00-roadmap.md:265 and :293, docs/roadmap.html:416 (outside the doc-lint corpus; only a gate-script row can pin it, precedent in the D48 script). Sites that stay true and must NOT be edited: docs/plans/implementation-plan.md:196, docs/plans/ci-cd-and-distribution.md:86, the D48 script's residual-id row, and the 2026-08-07 run-report. The live D-range sites: CLAUDE.md:17, ci-cd section 2.1(a) line 65, xtask/src/doc_lint.rs:455 (prose and tokenizer alternation on ONE line), and the RANGE_RE / RANGE_ALT_RE knobs of the five gate scripts, plus four prose headers above those knobs that rot silently (d46:62, d47:71, ub-lp9.25:109, d48:67). Two frozen historical D1..D48 strings must not be touched (docs/PRD.md:131 clause 10 and .unblock/issues.jsonl). docs/PROCESS.md:43 ("always the NEWEST script") and :51 (the knob list) go stale when a D49 script lands. Per precedent the D49 gate script lands with the IMPLEMENTATION commit and pins the D48 script's two knobs, which the self-row rule leaves unpinned today. The normative sentences to extend: docs/plans/01-design-spine.md:522 (names the from_code(err.to_string()) render path) and docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:94 (the error.rs row, whose test column promises only control-character sanitization).

INTERACTION WITH ub-kp7. Its recorded class covers both rmcp routes (:193 and :201), so a faithful interception would remove the live path that renders this message. The rendering fix still stands on its own (the variant stays constructible via an rmcp bump, a future demotion, or the test-util seam), but an end-to-end cell against a live frame would go vacuous the day ub-kp7 lands. The regression pin is therefore a unit cell over a test-util constructor that builds all four frame shapes.

Forks put to Miguel next: what the diagnostic prints (kind only; kind + method; kind + method + id; or a whole-string clip), whether the transport read gains a line cap here or in its own issue, and whether the rmcp post-handshake tracing dump is fixed here or tracked separately. Orchestrator rulings proposed alongside: every variant routes through one description function with a clipped pass-through wildcard; the D43 constant is reused rather than a second one minted; the duplicated marker literal in bulk_markdown is folded onto the constant; ship now, ahead of ub-kp7.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
DECIDE phase closed (2026-09-09). No separate Decide team ran: the Understand map already carried every option with its anchor and consequence, so the forks went straight to Miguel with the orchestrator's recommendations. Miguel resolved three forks and ratified four orchestrator rulings.

MIGUEL'S FORK RESOLUTIONS
1. What the startup-failure diagnostic says about a rejected first frame: the frame KIND, the METHOD name, and the envelope ID, each client-supplied member clipped by the D43 helper (crates/unblock-error/src/sanitize.rs clip, MAX_ECHOED_BYTES 128, marker appended); params, result, and the error body are NEVER rendered. Chosen over kind-only (no way to tell which client misbehaved), over kind plus method (loses correlation with the client's own log by id), and over clipping the whole Debug string (the cut lands inside rmcp's structural prefix and the multi-megabyte string is still built first).
2. A maximum accepted line length at the stdio transport (crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs:189-190, deliberately unbounded, rmcp parity) is OUT of this task. It changes what the server accepts, so it gets its own issue and, if taken, its own decision row.
3. rmcp's post-handshake tracing dump of every client frame in Debug (rmcp service.rs:985 at info, :942 at debug; live at a single -v because crates/unblock-cli/src/logging.rs:39 sets a global level floor) is OUT of this task. Different origin, opt-in verbosity; its own issue.

ORCHESTRATOR RULINGS, ratified
4. Every ServerInitializeError variant renders through ONE description function in crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs. The variant that carries the client frame gets the structural summary; the #[non_exhaustive] wildcard passes rmcp's own Display text through the same D43 clip, so a future variant that echoes client bytes is bounded on arrival, "Cancelled" stays byte-identical to the D38 doc comment at error.rs:62, and a real I/O error's text stays readable.
5. The D43 constant MAX_ECHOED_BYTES is REUSED; no second echo bound is minted for this diagnostic.
6. The hard-coded "…[truncated]" literal in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/bulk_markdown.rs:129 is folded onto unblock_error::TRUNCATION_MARKER (no behaviour change; that file's 80-char header bound is untouched), and the marker's value is written into the unblock-error crate plan so it is a stated contract rather than two free-drifting copies.
7. Ship now, ahead of ub-kp7. The regression pin is a unit cell over a test-util constructor that builds ExpectedInitializeRequest for all four frame shapes (Request, Notification, Response, Error) with oversized id, method, params, result and error.message, asserting the rendered message length is bounded and that no params byte appears. An end-to-end cell against a live frame may be added as a bonus but is not the pin, because ub-kp7 will make that path vacuous.

DECISION IDENTITY: a NEW D-id (D49), as PRD D48 clause 6(ii) already rules ("under its own decision"). Consequences: reciprocal cross-references on D47 clause 8(iii) and D48 clause 6(ii); the D-range bump D1..D48 -> D1..D49 at every live site (the PROCESS section 3 list, plus the four gate-script prose headers that rot silently); no CONTRACT_VERSION move (unblock.mcp.v1.9 stands, CONTRACT_HASH digests only capabilities and schema); no new ErrorCode; exit codes unmoved. The D49 gate script and its CI step land with the IMPLEMENTATION commit, per the D45-D48 precedent, and pin the D48 script's two range knobs.

Next: Spec/Plan (the spec-first doc cascade as one commit on branch ub-b1a-debug-bytes-bound), then the design Review gate.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
SPEC/PLAN phase (2026-09-09). Team: an architect drafted the D49 row and the normative sentences, a project-manager wrote the exact 28-row cascade checklist, a single spec writer applied both in an isolated worktree as ONE commit, and a coordinator checked the diff against the checklist and the decisions. Branch ub-b1a-debug-bytes-bound (spec-first; the commit is being amended before the design Review gate, so the sha is reported in the gate comment).

WHAT LANDED, 15 files, doc-only plus one comment line. docs/PRD.md gains the D49 row on one physical line after D48, with reciprocal inline notes on D47 clause 8(iii) and D48 clause 6(ii) (ub-b1a closed by D49; D48 clause 3's byte-for-byte payload guarantee stated unaffected). The spine extends the section 2.4 sentence that names the from_code(InternalError, err.to_string()) render path and adds one sentence to the sanitization-chokepoint paragraph saying length bounding is per origin (D43 at the argument seam, D49 at the startup diagnostic) and the chokepoint governs control characters only. The unblock-mcp crate plan's error.rs row gains the description function, the test-util constructor, and the test column (four-shape pin, Cancelled byte-identity pin, the >128-byte clip pin, the ordering pin, the mutation list); its bulk_markdown.rs row records the marker fold. The unblock-error crate plan's sanitize.rs row states TRUNCATION_MARKER's value as a contract (U+2026 plus eleven ASCII bytes, 14 bytes, 12 chars). The implementation plan gains block T3.12 (the next free top-level id, a peer of T3.11) with ten acceptance criteria. DESIGN REVIEW GATE, round 1 (2026-09-09): FAIL, back to Spec/Plan. Spec commit 9072bd6 on branch ub-b1a-debug-bytes-bound (the coordinator-check repairs were amended in before the gate). Four adversarial lenses (design soundness, implementability against rmcp source, doc cascade and false claims, test adequacy), each in its own worktree, plus a coordinator; all four failed it independently. The first attempt at this round died on the session limit after the repair agent finished; the gate itself ran on the resumed workflow with the repair result cached.

WHAT PASSED. The cascade is clean: the range bump landed at every live site, the frozen historical strings did not move, the reciprocal notes are reciprocal, doc-lint and all six gate scripts are green, and roughly forty file:line anchors resolve exactly.

THE MUST-FIXES, in plain words, with the orchestrator's ruling where one was needed.
1. The row claims no variant sent through the wildcard reaches the 128-byte clip. False for TransportError: rmcp renders it as "Send message error Transport [<type name>] error: <io text>", where the type name is std::any::type_name of the transport (rmcp transport.rs:130-132, 240-245), over 98 bytes on its own, so the clip would cut inside the type name and hide the I/O reason. RULED: a dedicated arm renders the context and the INNER error (DynamicTransportError's public error field), each clipped, without the type name, which carries no operator value. The wildcard keeps the pass-through for the rest.
2. "No shipped cell inverts" is false under the row as written: emit_diagnostic_writes_the_error_line (crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:435-457) asserts the line contains "connection reset". Under ruling 1 the inner text survives, so that cell stays green and becomes the named pin that the transport arm keeps the I/O reason.
3. The literal grammar writes a request "<method>" with hand-written quotes while the same clause mandates the Rust string Debug of the clipped member, which supplies its own quotes. RULED: the grammar is spelled in the Debug convention for every string-valued member (a request "tools/list" with id 7; a request "x/y" with id "abc…[truncated]"; a notification "notifications/cancelled"; a response to id 1; an error response to id "k"; an error response with no id; no frame arrived).
4. The wildcard's quoting was never ruled, and the Cancelled byte-identity forbids quoting there. RULED: the wildcard and the transport arm clip rmcp's own Display WITHOUT Debug quoting, because that text is rmcp's sentence and not a client member; its bound is clip then the section 2.4 chokepoint.
5. "The whole expansion happens at one site" is false on the wildcard arm (control bytes still expand at sanitize_message). Scope that sentence and the exact-ceiling claim to the ExpectedInitializeRequest arms.
6. The "no byte count for the fixed prefix" note quotes measurements of the OLD rmcp prefix that D49 deletes; the new fixed text per arm is countable. Count it per arm; move the old numbers to the naive-clip rationale.
7. "Bounded on the side clause (2) names" names no side at two sites (the PRD row's tests clause and the T3.12 criterion). Name BOUND TWO, the rendered Debug-escaped member.
8. Two counts are wrong (four scripts carry the contract knob, not five; three snapshots carry the version, not two). Give the lists, no counts.
9. "Every gate row had zero matches on the pre-fix tree" is false for the contract-knob row (pinned unmoved) and the ub-b1a row (already in the export). Scope the duty to rows asserting new landings; define the pre-fix tree as the tree at the spec commit.
10. The code rows of the gate script are not classified; the clip use in error.rs and the marker use in bulk_markdown.rs can be satisfied by a doc comment, so they are line-anchored rows, not presence rows.
11. The marker pin is a tautology (asserting the header ends with the constant compares the constant with itself). RULED: the shipped cell at bulk_markdown.rs:832-843 KEEPS its literal assertion, which is what makes the fold observable, and unblock-error gains a cell pinning TRUNCATION_MARKER's value, length 14 bytes and 12 chars. This also closes the unblock-error crate-plan promise (must-fix 15).
12. The four-shape cell's oversized members are not distributed per shape, and rmcp forbids most on most shapes. Name them per shape: Request (method, string id, params); Notification (method, params); Response (string id, result); Error (string id, error.message, error.data).
13. "Matches the grammar" plus "not one byte of params" is not a killing pair. Require assert_eq! against the full expected message, with a distinct sentinel per member.
14. Three grammar arms have no cell (no frame arrived; error response with no id; numeric id through Display), and error.data is never in a negative. Add them.
15. See 11.
16. The test-util constructor is declared without pub; its three siblings are pub fn, and a private hidden fn is dead code under deny(warnings). Write pub fn.
17. The gate-script row list omits the three self-wiring rows every sibling carries (the ci-cd paragraph, the ci.yml step, the PROCESS section 3 list). Add them.

SHOULD-FIXES (fifteen), all taken: the version-clamp anchor (the rewrite is clamp_unsupported_initialize_version at server.rs:551-560, not the struct at :504); drop the "three quotations" count; "avoids a SECOND full copy" instead of "materialises"; a future echoing variant is bounded in output not allocation and still earns its own arm; distinct labels for the two prefixes; scope the universal quoting sentence to string-valued members; name std::error::Error::source() as a third latent non-route (nothing walks the chain today); say InitializeFailed and UnexpectedInitializeResponse are unreachable rather than short; append the D49 sentence to the roadmap's v1.0.1 crate-matrix note; carry the ci-cd class-(a) example to D49; state D48 clause 3 as a cross-sink byte equality D49 preserves; give the ordering pin its byte offset; the wildcard is a single arm and the cell pins that arm; state that the tracker re-export lands in the Track commit of the same PR and CI evaluates the PR head.

Round 2 runs next: the same repairer amends the single spec commit, then the same four lenses re-gate with the round-1 verdict in hand. A second FAIL escalates to Miguel (PROCESS section 5). Full round-1 verdict in the session scratchpad; the must-fixes above are the durable record.
