description:
Split out of ub-og3 by Miguel's decision at its Decide phase (2026-08-06), fork "Debug bytes". docs/PRD.md D47 clause 8(iii) names this in the SAME sentence as the stdout-channel defect ub-og3 fixes; moving the stream does not sanitise the content, so ub-og3 would otherwise close clause 8(iii) by half. This issue carries the other half.

PRIORITY RAISED and this section added 2026-08-07, after the ub-og3 Verify gate raised the sink question and the orchestrator MEASURED the amplification. Miguel re-confirmed the scoping: the clip stays OUT of ub-og3, but the consequence is disclosed rather than left implicit.

MEASURED AMPLIFICATION, one spawn per case, against the D48 binary: a first frame whose method name is N bytes produces N bytes on stderr, one for one, with no cap.
  method 1,000 bytes      -> stdout 0 bytes, stderr 1,422 bytes
  method 100,000 bytes    -> stdout 0 bytes, stderr 100,422 bytes
  method 5,000,000 bytes  -> stdout 0 bytes, stderr 5,000,422 bytes

WHY D48 MAKES THIS MORE URGENT RATHER THAN LESS, even though it amplifies nothing. Before D48 those bytes went to stdout, equally unbounded — so the VOLUME is unchanged and D48 is not the cause. What changed is the SINK. Under the D31 child-per-client topology an MCP host normally captures the child's stderr into its own logs, which PERSIST; an unparseable line on the framing channel was transient, and a client would choke on it and move on. So the same attacker-controlled volume now lands somewhere more durable. That is a consequence of a correct fix, not a defect of it, and the D48 decision row states it rather than leaving a reader to discover it.

WHAT IT IS. When the handshake fails, the message rendered into the failure report is rmcp's own error Display, which embeds a Rust `Debug` rendering of the frame the client sent. Measured verbatim off main at 7790db0:

  mcp server error: failed to start the MCP server: expect initialized request, but received: Some(Notification(JsonRpcNotification { jsonrpc: JsonRpcVersion2_0, notification: CustomNotification(CustomNotification { method: "notifications/cancelled", params: None, extensions: Extensions }) }))

The method name — and, on other shapes, the params — are client-supplied.

WHAT IS ALREADY MITIGATED, and what is not. `StructuredError::from_code` routes the message through `sanitize_message` (crates/unblock-error/src/sanitize.rs:85-114), which escapes control characters, keeping only newline and tab. So terminal-escape and control-character injection are already handled. What is NOT handled: there is no LENGTH cap and no structural reduction.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS. NOT in crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs, which only serialises an already-built payload and contains no `Debug` formatting at all. The message is formed upstream at rmcp service/server.rs:53-54 flowing into crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs:34-41. An earlier version of this issue anchored it at the serialiser; that was wrong and the ub-og3 design Review gate corrected it.

DECIDE: whether the remedy is a length cap on the rendered message, a structural summary of the offending frame (kind plus method, no params) instead of the `Debug` blob, or an explicit ruling that escaping alone is sufficient. The third answer remains legitimate — but it must be RULED, not left implicit, and it is harder to defend now that the destination is a durable log.

RELATION TO ub-og3. Independent of it: ub-og3 moves this message from stdout to stderr and changes not one byte of its content.
title: Bug: the mcp startup-failure message embeds an unbounded Rust `Debug` rendering of attacker-controlled frame bytes

description:
Found by the ub-og3 design Review gate (2026-08-06) and split out by Miguel's ruling at that gate. It is the SIBLING of ub-og3, in the same crate, one function away — and it is LATENT, not live.

WHAT IT IS. `crates/unblock-cli/src/output.rs:147-157` (`emit_report`) writes the rendered structured report to `std::io::stdout()` UNCONDITIONALLY. It takes no notion of whether the running command owns stdout as a protocol channel — the very notion D48 introduces one function away, in `exit.rs`, for the error path.

WHY IT IS NOT LIVE TODAY. Verified at the gate: `crates/unblock-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs` contains no `output::` call at all, and `emit_report`'s four callers are `version`, `doctor`, `init` and `migrate` — every one of them a command whose stdout is an ordinary report stream. So no shipped path can reach it from a stdout-owning command, and ub-og3 does not fix it because there is nothing there to fix yet.

WHY IT IS STILL A DEFECT WORTH A RECORD. D48 states its rule over a PROPERTY — a subcommand whose stdout is a protocol channel — precisely so a future such command inherits the rule instead of re-deriving it. The error path will then be safe by construction (the exhaustive match forces the author to classify the command) while the REPORT path silently is not. That is this same defect, re-opened, for whoever adds that command.

WHY DOCUMENT-ONLY WAS REJECTED as the remedy: a normative constraint carried only by a code comment has no test, no lint and no issue behind it — deleting the comment is invisible. Miguel ruled it gets a record instead, named in the D48 decision row alongside ub-kp7 and ub-b1a.

REMEDY WHEN IT IS TAKEN: give `emit_report` the same role parameter the D48 seam gives `into_exit`, or make it structurally unreachable from a stdout-owning command. Decide which at that point; do not assume the first.
title: Bug (latent): `output::emit_report` writes structured reports to stdout with no notion of a command that owns stdout

close_reason: Merged to main via PR 438 (2026-08-06, rebase-merge, tip 7790db0) as decision D47. A JSON-RPC frame whose envelope id cannot be decoded is now answered -32600 Invalid Request on the id recovered from the raw bytes — omitted when they are ambiguous — and DROPPED, instead of falling through the untagged message union into a notification and vanishing. The class closed is the whole un-decodable-id class, not just the duplicate: a null id, a wrongly-typed id and a number outside what the request-id type accepts were each silent too, and duplication was the minority route. A frame with NO id stays silent, deliberately and verifiably. Pre-handshake the same frame used to kill the process with a non-JSON-RPC blob on the framing channel; it is now answered and the connection goes on to serve a full handshake. Contract-neutral: no new error code, frozen version and hash unmoved. Two gates, six rounds in total; 26 of 26 catalogue mutants killed with zero survivors plus about 30 more across two lenses; all 19 CI checks green. Residuals disclosed rather than claimed closed: ub-nbz (the reply is lost when the dependency cancels our read future under concurrent traffic — pre-existing, the shipped parse-error arm behaves identically), ub-788 (that parse-error arm still omits a readable id), ub-og3 (the stdout framing-channel blob, of which this change removes one route). ub-q1u was found in passing and is unrelated.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand phase started (2026-08-05) — taken as the active v1.0.1 patch-slot item, off main at bd39fa2.

ORCHESTRATOR ORIENTATION FIRST, so the team is briefed on measured facts rather than the issue's original hypothesis. A raw-bytes stdio probe was run against the current main binary (a normal client library cannot express a duplicate member at all), one frame per case after a real handshake. Reproduced: a frame carrying the request id twice gets NO response whatsoever, and this holds whether the two ids are identical or different, and on a tool call, on ping, and on a tools listing with no parameters member at all. The connection survives — a clean ping immediately afterwards is answered normally, so nothing desynchronises; the frame simply vanishes.

THE ISSUE'S SEVERITY FRAMING IS NOW BOUNDED, and downwards. A duplicated-id frame carrying an issue-creation payload produced no response AND created nothing; a follow-up listing came back empty. So the silenced frame is DROPPED, not executed. This is an availability and protocol-conformance defect, not a second execution defect like the one D43 closed.

FOUR RESULTS THE ISSUE DID NOT PREDICT, and they widen the question rather than settle it. Duplicating the method member, or the jsonrpc member, produces an out-of-band parse error with the id OMITTED — which is a diagnostic, but a client correlating strictly by id has still received nothing for its request, so the issue's fifth acceptance criterion may be violated by more than the id case. Duplicating the parameters member on a ping was ANSWERED SUCCESSFULLY, which appears to contradict a comment shipped with D43 asserting that shape is a hard parse error for both parsers. And a duplicate INSIDE the parameters — the exact class D43 exists to reject in-band — came back as a method-not-found error instead, escaping the in-band channel; an earlier gate classified that as an already-disclosed residual rather than a bypass, and I have asked for that judgement to be re-derived independently rather than inherited, because if an envelope shape can carry a duplicate past the D43 gate that is a security finding outranking this whole task.

Understand team spawned as a Workflow (three adversarial lenses plus a coordinator), read-only, with the standing instruction that any claim must carry either a file-and-line citation or the probe bytes that prove it. (1) DECODER MECHANISM — read the rmcp message enum in the vendored source and establish why a duplicated id vanishes while a duplicated method is a parse error and a duplicated parameters member succeeds; then answer the question the issue explicitly asks, whether duplication is the ONLY route into this silent reinterpretation, by probing the neighbourhood (unknown extra envelope members, a null id, wrongly-typed ids, batch frames, a missing or wrong jsonrpc value); deliver a truth table with every row marked as probed or derived from source. (2) BLAST RADIUS — what a real client actually does when nothing arrives (rmcp's own client pending-request handling, read from source), whether the omitted-id parse error also leaves a request pending, whether repetition accumulates anything server-side, whether a hung client can hold the write lock or a claim hostage, and an honest judgement of who could emit such a frame at all. (3) SPEC AND CONTRACT — what JSON-RPC 2.0, the underlying JSON specification and the MCP specification actually require, quoted verbatim; which of our own normative sentences are false or unqualified while this stands, including the D43 code comments treated as contract prose; the candidate response channels with their spec basis and cost; and the full documentation cascade a fix would trigger under this repo's own decision rules.

The team analyses only — no design, no implementation. Its output feeds a Decide fork for Miguel, then spec-first, then Implement and the two gates.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand outcome (2026-08-05; three adversarial lenses — decoder mechanism, blast radius, spec and contract — plus a coordinator that re-verified every load-bearing claim against source rather than aggregating the lenses' word). The map lands in the run-report at Track time; what follows is what a decision now depends on.

THE MECHANISM IS ESTABLISHED, and it is not what the issue's title says. The message union rmcp decodes into is untagged, with the request variant tried before the notification variant, and the notification variant has no id field at all while no rmcp struct forbids unknown members. So ANY frame whose id member fails to decode falls through to the notification variant, the surplus id landing harmlessly in a catch-all; rmcp then has no response obligation and our server registers no notification handler, so the frame evaporates. Confirmed live from the server's own debug stream: a duplicated-id tool call is logged as a custom notification carrying the tool payload, and nothing else happens.

DUPLICATION IS THE MINORITY ROUTE, which is the finding that most changes this task's shape. Verified by my own probe run: an id that is null, a bare object, a boolean, an integer beyond the 64-bit range, or the JSON number written as an exponent are each silently swallowed with no duplicate anywhere in the frame — the same number written plainly is answered normally. The id type accepted is only an integer representable in 64 bits, or a string. The honest class predicate is "the bytes carried an id and the decode produced a notification", not "a duplicate exists". A frame with NO id is a notification and its silence is correct — that case must stay out of any fix.

THE PARSE-ERROR CASES ARE NOT THE SAFER HALF, contrary to what my own orientation comment implied. Our transport passes no id when it emits the parse error, unconditionally, even when the raw bytes carry a perfectly readable one; and rmcp's CLIENT drops an error response that has no id, while its request future has no timeout at all. So the duplicated-method and duplicated-jsonrpc frames hang an rmcp client exactly as hard as the silent ones — they differ only in leaving a byte a human can see in a log. The fifth acceptance criterion is therefore violated by two classes, not one.

A THIRD SILENCE EXISTS AND IT IS DELIBERATE. Our own forked compatibility filter drops an id-carrying frame whose method starts with the notifications prefix and whose parameters rmcp cannot type — on purpose, pinned by a test, because rmcp drops it and the fork exists to match rmcp byte for byte. That collides head-on with the fifth acceptance criterion as written: satisfying it literally means deliberately diverging from rmcp, which is the very thing the fork's differential harness exists to prevent.

NO SECURITY FINDING, and it was re-derived from source rather than inherited from the earlier gate. The method-not-found case is the already-disclosed non-executing residual: a duplicate of a key the typed tool-call parameters name kills that variant, the catch-all request variant accepts it, and rmcp's default handler answers method-not-found — no execution, proven on the wire by creating nothing. No frame in any of these classes was ever executed. One honest sharpening for the record: on a silenced frame the D43 verdict IS computed and stamped, and then never consulted, because the gate sits on the request path; it is inert only because we register no notification handler, which is a structural note for whoever adds one.

A WORSE VARIANT, previously undocumented anywhere, which the team could only assert and I verified myself: PRE-HANDSHAKE the same frame is FATAL. As the first message on the connection it makes rmcp fail with "expect initialized request", the process exits 1 — and the structured error is written to STDOUT, i.e. onto the JSON-RPC framing channel, as a non-JSON-RPC blob. A clean non-initialize request in the same position is answered normally and exits 0, so the trigger is precisely the degradation to a notification. This reaches D40's teardown contract and is currently documented nowhere.

FALSE OR UNQUALIFIED CLAIMS WE ALREADY SHIP, all re-verified: the spine's envelope sentence enumerates which duplicated envelope members hard-fail as if the list were closed — it omits id entirely, and its claim about the parameters member is method-dependent, not absolute (a duplicated parameters member on ping is answered SUCCESSFULLY, while the same duplication on a tool call or a tools listing is a parse error). The scanner's own doc asserts such a frame "is rejected upstream anyway", which is false for methods that take no parameters, and asserts a duplicate elsewhere in the envelope is "a different, already non-executing class", which is falsified by our own shipped test: a duplicate inside an UNKNOWN envelope member executes the tool normally (I reproduced it — an issue was created). A transport test comment states as a transport-wide invariant that a request outside the notifications prefix is never ignored because the client is waiting on its id; this class violates it. The D43 decision row's rationale for deferring — "there is no request id to answer on, and an out-of-band reply would contradict the in-band clause" — is wrong on both halves: with two identical occurrences the bytes carry one unambiguous id, and the transport already emits out-of-band parse errors today. And the roadmap carries no row for this issue although the decision row says it is tracked in the same patch slot.

EXTERNAL SPECS, fetched and quoted rather than remembered. The underlying JSON specification only SHOULD-recommends unique member names and explicitly says behaviour on duplicates is unpredictable, naming last-wins, error and report-all as all-observed — so last-wins is not non-conforming, it is merely one of three. JSON-RPC 2.0 says nothing at all about duplicate members; it defines a notification as a request WITHOUT an id member and forbids replying to one — which is exactly why a frame that HAS id members is not a notification and the no-reply exemption does not cover it. Its invalid-request code is defined as "The JSON sent is not a valid Request object", which fits this class precisely. And it states that when there was an error detecting the id, the response id MUST be null — a MUST that our shipped assertion deliberately contradicts by omitting the id instead, following the newer MCP guidance rmcp itself cites. That conflict is real and is part of what Miguel now decides.

Forks going to Miguel now: the scope of the class to close, the response channel and its id form, whether the deliberate parity drop is an acceptance-criterion violation or the criterion is to be re-scoped, and where the pre-handshake fatal variant belongs.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Decide (2026-08-05) — Miguel resolved all four forks, and took the recommendation on each.

SCOPE = THE WHOLE UN-DECODABLE-ID CLASS, not duplication alone. The binding predicate is: the raw bytes carried a top-level request id AND the decode produced a notification. That covers the duplicated id, a null id, an id of the wrong JSON type, and a number outside what the id type accepts — the exponent form of an integer among them, which is silent while the same value written plainly is answered. A frame with NO id stays untouched: it is a legitimate notification and its silence is correct. Closing only the duplicate would have let this issue close asserting that no frame leaves a client waiting, while five reproduced shapes still did.

CHANNEL = an out-of-band invalid-request error, answered ON THE RECOVERED ID where the bytes yield one unambiguously, falling back to a null id where they do not. Unambiguous means a single id that merely failed to type, or several occurrences that are all equal; two different ids, or a value that is not a representable id at all, take the null fallback. The reason this beat the two cheaper forms is not aesthetic: an rmcp client DROPS an error that carries no id and its request future has no timeout, so an id-less reply leaves the caller stuck exactly as the silence does — it only adds a byte a human can see. The invalid-request code is also the literally correct one, defined in the spec as "the JSON sent is not a valid Request object". Declined: always-null (the letter of the spec's MUST, but it does not unblock the caller and contradicts our own pinned assertion), always-omitted (consistent with our existing parse-error arm and with the newer MCP guidance, but same failure to unblock), and ratifying the silence (no spec basis — the no-reply exemption is for notifications, and these frames HAVE id members).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 5 IS RE-SCOPED to "no frame that rmcp itself would answer may go unanswered". This was forced, not cosmetic: our forked compatibility filter deliberately drops an id-carrying frame whose method starts with the notifications prefix and whose parameters rmcp cannot type, pinned by a test, because the fork exists to match rmcp byte for byte. Satisfying the old wording literally would have meant deliberately diverging from rmcp — the exact thing the differential harness exists to prevent. The happy structural consequence, which the plan must verify rather than assume: that frame is never delivered as a message at all, so a predicate keyed on a delivered notification cannot see it and needs no special case.

THE PRE-HANDSHAKE FATAL VARIANT splits. Its removal rides this fix (if the transport answers and does not deliver, rmcp never sees a notification in the initialize slot and does not die — to be confirmed, not assumed). The separate defect of writing a non-JSON-RPC blob onto stdout, the framing channel, is now ub-og3 with the reproduction and the exact code path recorded.

TWO ISSUES OPENED so nothing stays implicit. ub-og3 as above. And ub-788 for the residual I am NOT allowed to hide: the parse-error arm omits a readable id unconditionally, so the duplicated-method and duplicated-jsonrpc frames still leave an rmcp client pending forever. Miguel scoped that out of this fix; it is blocked on this one landing, because that is where the id-recovery machinery and the re-specified byte-identity contract get built. It must be disclosed as a residual in the decision row and the spine, in the same honest way the D43 row disclosed this issue — never claimed closed.

ORCHESTRATOR'S DECISION-ID CALL, open to countermand: this rides a NEW decision id, D47, not an inline amendment to D43. Two reasons. The class decided here is not the duplicate-key class — duplication is the minority route into it, and most of the shapes carry no duplicate anywhere. And the channel decision REVERSES D43's sixth clause, which deferred this saying there was no id to answer on and that an out-of-band reply would contradict its in-band clause; the Understand phase falsified both halves, since identical occurrences yield one unambiguous id and the transport already emits out-of-band parse errors today. Under the process rule that is a separately-motivated decision, so: reciprocal cross-references on both rows, and the decision-range bump from D1..D46 to D1..D47 at every site the rule enumerates — the three prose sites plus the live-range knobs of the three shipped required check scripts — landing in the SPEC commit.

Spec/Plan phase in flight as a Workflow: an empirical probe settling the design unknowns first (the detection predicate and whether the existing scanner can distinguish equal from differing duplicate occurrences; the per-line cost of one more parse, given this path is already documented as unbounded; whether answering really does prevent the pre-handshake death; the false-positive surface of real notifications that carry an id; what the byte-identity harness must become; and whether any of this touches the frozen GA contract), then three planners in parallel — code design, spec text plus the full document cascade, and a verification plan where every test cell must name the mutant it kills — then a coordinator that writes one package and is told to hunt for the specific failure this repo has seen before: three internally-consistent plans that contradict each other at the seams.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Spec/Plan outcome (2026-08-05; an empirical probe first, then three planners — code design, spec text plus cascade, verification — then a coordinator that wrote one package and was told to hunt for internally-consistent plans contradicting each other at the seams). Package complete and marked ready for the design gate.

THE DESIGN, in short. A new crate-private module in the MCP crate exposes a three-state envelope-id verdict — absent, recovered, unusable — computed by a deserializer seed that walks ONLY the root object, compares DECODED keys (so an escaped spelling of the key cannot slip past a byte comparison), keeps at most one candidate without short-circuiting (so a trailing occurrence cannot be missed), and delegates the type check to rmcp's own request-id deserializer rather than reimplementing it. It is consulted inside the transport's existing delivery arm, where the raw line is still borrowed, behind an EXHAUSTIVE match on the message kind rather than a pattern test — so a future rmcp variant becomes a compile error instead of a silent hole. Absent is a no-op, which is the carve-out for the legitimate notification and leaves those bytes untouched. Otherwise the transport answers the invalid-request error and DROPS the frame; answer-and-drop is what removes the pre-handshake death, and delivering as well was measured to remain fatal. Both replies go through a single new helper that the existing parse-error arm is refactored onto, so the two out-of-band arms are identical by construction and the write half still encodes through rmcp's own codec. The D43 scan, its stamping and its gate are code-untouched and provably disjoint, the gate being request-only. Nothing below the top layer changes, no new dependency, and the frozen contract version and hash do not move.

AN IMPOSSIBILITY WAS ESCALATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED, and it is the single most valuable thing this phase produced. Miguel's channel decision said the ambiguous case falls back to a null id. That cannot be written through rmcp's type: its error message's id field is an option with skip-if-none, so no value of it serializes as an explicit null — only omitted, or a concrete id. I verified this in the dependency source myself. The rmcp comment beside it cites the MCP specification's error-responses section, which says the id is omitted precisely when the server cannot read it. MIGUEL RATIFIED "OMITTED" for the fallback: the arm that carries the decision's substance — answering on the recovered id — ships exactly as decided, and in the ambiguous case no correct id exists to answer on, so null versus omitted cannot unblock anyone and is pure form. The alternative was hand-writing the bytes around rmcp's codec, which would have destroyed the property that our emitted bytes are identical to rmcp's by construction rather than by test, and turned a shipped assertion red against our own output.

MIGUEL ALSO RATIFIED minting an executable claims-check script for this decision, as the three preceding decisions each did. Not cunning: this change retires live prose in at least six files, and this repo has watched derived claims rot when nothing executable pinned them. The cost is a required lint step, a normative paragraph, and knob rows in the three sibling scripts, all from its first commit.

THREE SEAM CONFLICTS THE COORDINATOR CAUGHT, which is exactly what it was convened for. The first would have shipped test cells asserting the OPPOSITE of the design: the design specified a descriptive message constant while the verification plan wrote about twenty byte-exact expectations against a different literal — the cells would have gone red against the design and the natural repair would have been to weaken the design. The second is subtler and matters more: the verification plan claimed a shipped cell is "guaranteed red on main today", and it is not — that cell's frame carries two DIFFERING ids, so under the new behaviour it takes the omitted arm and both its assertions stay true. Only its PROSE becomes false. A reader acting on the stated reason would have expected a red cell, not seen one, and concluded the fix was not installed. It is split into two cells, one genuinely red on main and one preserving the shipped negatives. The third corrected a claim about where a heading lives, in the direction of MORE work: the planner was wrong about that line, and the line carries two OTHER claims this change falsifies.

THE HONEST GAPS the package declares rather than hides: no gate command was actually run this pass (the coordinator has no shell), a dozen divergence-corpus entries were never individually confirmed silent on main and must be replayed before the fix lands, one arm of the verdict has no end-to-end witness frame and is unit-covered only with that said out loud in its own docstring, and one failure mode — the write guard being held across the next read — is pinned by no cell at all and is flagged as a review item.

Design Review gate spawning now: three adversarial lenses plus a coordinator, over the package, with the standing instruction to hunt for a bypass rather than confirm the design, to re-derive the claims the package itself marks unverified, and to judge whether the verification plan is genuinely non-vacuous — the realistic failure here is a green suite proving nothing, and every cell in the package is required to name the one-line mutant it kills.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design Review gate, round 1 (2026-08-05; three adversarial lenses — bypass hunt, architecture and contract, verification non-vacuity — plus a coordinator that confirmed every blocking item at its own site before admitting it): VERDICT = PASS WITH MUST-FIXES. Ten items, all corrections to the package; no redesign is asked for.

Note for the record: this gate had to be run twice. The first attempt died entirely — all four agents hit the session limit before producing anything — and was relaunched from the saved script once the limit reset. Nothing partial was written and no artefact was disturbed.

NO BYPASS, and the coordinator is explicit that this is a result rather than a gap in effort. Three lenses hunted independently and none constructed a frame inside the decided scope that the predicate fails to see. Facts re-derived by the coordinator itself rather than taken from a lens: rmcp's message union really has exactly four variants and is NOT marked non-exhaustive, so the exhaustive production match compiles today and turns into a compile error on a version bump — which is the design's own tripwire working; the request and response variants name a non-optional id, so a malformed id structurally cannot produce them; batch and array roots, non-UTF-8, byte-order-marked, carriage-returned, whitespace-only and over-deep frames all end as parse errors and never become notifications; the byte-order-mark assumption the new scan turns on holds, because the transport strips the newline and carriage return early but the mark only later, inside the parse helper; the refactor of the existing parse-error arm preserves both of its exit conditions and its recover-on-the-next-line behaviour; and the deliberate parity drops are outside the decided predicate by wording, not by accident of implementation.

THE VERIFICATION PLAN IS NOT VACUOUS AS A WHOLE — delete the fix and twenty-two byte-exact divergence cells plus a dozen others go red. What failed is a set of claims, which is precisely the defect class this repo keeps hitting.

THE FOUR THAT MATTER. First, and it is the one that changed a decision: the decision-row draft asserts that nothing in this class ever executed and that the change rejects nothing the general-availability release accepted. BOTH ARE FALSE. A cancellation notification carrying an un-decodable envelope id is recognised inside rmcp's serve loop, before any handler of ours runs, and cancels the matching in-flight request — so that one shape does execute something today, and answering-and-dropping removes it. Second, the recovered-id arm is reachable ONLY through repeated EQUAL occurrences: the custom request and notification decoders are byte-identical and the request variant is tried first, so a single well-formed id can never reach the notification variant. Every other shape takes the omitted arm, which an rmcp client DROPS — answered, but the caller still not released. Nothing in the package said so. Third, the decided comparator is decoded-VALUE equality and NO cell pinned it: every equal pair in the corpus is byte-identical, so an implementation that retained raw byte spans instead of decoded values would pass the entire suite while violating the design and leaving a client hanging. That is the package's own argument about escaped KEYS, not applied to VALUES. Fourth, two cells claim mutants they cannot kill — one because the frame's on-the-wire bytes never contain the window that mutant filters on, so the cell stays green under its own designated mutant.

THE REST are cascade completeness: two normative CLOSED enumerations that this decision falsifies were missing from the cascade; the published rendered roadmap carries one bullet per decision in its patch-release card and is pinned positively by two required scripts, while the package deferred it as unverified; the new claims-check script's obligations were incomplete on four counts and backwards on one (the precedent is that the NEWEST script pins the OLDER siblings' knobs, not the reverse); and the package still filed two of Miguel's already-binding decisions as open forks, which a design gate cannot ship — an open fork in a package invites an implementer to build a toggle.

THE COORDINATOR ALSO WORKED IN THE HONEST DIRECTION, which is worth recording: it REFUSED six lens claims as blocking and said why for each — including one where it had no shell and declined to rest a must-fix on provenance reasoning it could not check, one where a lens wanted to name tracker ids for residuals Miguel never minted (which would plant dangling references in the interface specification), one where a lens wanted a test cell that would require a timeout the package's own rules forbid, and one where a lens listed two sites as falsified when the underlying principle at those sites survives and editing them would damage a correct statement. It also verified that no lens proposed softening any binding decision or narrowing the scope back to duplication alone.

MIGUEL RULED on the one item escalated to him: THE LOST CANCELLATION IS DISCLOSED, NOT PRESERVED. A conforming cancellation, which carries no id at all, is unaffected; the frame that loses its effect is malformed. Preserving it would mean delivering the frame after answering it, for that one shape — which is exactly what re-opens the pre-handshake fatality that answering-and-dropping removes. The decision row will now NAME that shape as the single one in the class that executed anything, and disclose the removal as a reasoned consequence.

A CONSEQUENCE MIGUEL SHOULD SEE, following from the second finding above and from the impossibility he already ratified: the benefit of answering on a recovered id — actually releasing a waiting caller — applies to the repeated-equal-id shape. The other shapes get an answer whose id is omitted, which an rmcp client discards, so those callers get a diagnostic on the connection rather than a resolution. There is no better option available: the only way to answer them at all would be the explicit-null form, which the dependency's type cannot serialize, and silence is strictly worse.

Revision round in flight: a single reviser applies all ten (single writer, because the package must stay internally coherent), keeping a change log, followed by a focused two-lens delta-verify that rules on each item as landed, weakened or not landed, and hunts for defects the revision itself introduced. Under the two-iteration rule, a failure there escalates rather than loops.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design Review gate CLOSED (2026-08-05). Round 1 = PASS WITH MUST-FIXES (ten items) → single-writer revision → delta-verify = FAIL on three defects the revision itself introduced → escalated to Miguel under the two-iteration rule → Miguel authorised the orchestrator to close them directly → closed and verified. Implement is now in flight.

THE DELTA-VERIFY CONFIRMED ALL TEN LANDED AND NOTHING WAS SOFTENED, checked at each site rather than aggregated, with the load-bearing facts re-derived from the dependency source: the cancellation really is performed inside the serve loop upstream of the handler spawn; the custom request and notification decoders really do have identical bodies, which is what makes the recovered-id arm reachable only through repeated equal occurrences; and the transport really does compute the existing duplicate-key verdict before the parse, which is why the reviewer's own suggested repair for one mutant could not have compiled and the reviser was right to refuse it. The anti-softening pass came back clean at every binding decision, and three of them are now strictly stronger than before — decoded-value equality is normative rather than implied, the deliberate parity drop is stated as a structural consequence rather than a concession, and the scope predicate names duplication as the minority route at all six sites that state it.

WHY IT FAILED ANYWAY, and the pattern is worth recording because it is the third time this session: each of the three defects sat INSIDE the repair of its own item. First, the new zero-live-hits directive could not pass — the phrase it forbids occurs twice, and the second occurrence is a NEGATED use in the product-requirements document whose subject is the argument boundary, not the envelope id, so this change does not falsify it; encoded as written it would have turned a required lint step permanently red on a correct sentence and pointed a sweeper at the top document of the hierarchy. Second, the mutation protocol still instructed the implementer to measure up to mutant twenty-three while the catalogue had grown to twenty-four — excluding precisely the two mutants added to close the gate's two coverage findings, including the only one that fails on a raw-span value comparator, which was the whole bypass the finding existed to close. Third, the repaired coverage sentence re-certified a cell as graded on a justification that is false at the dependency source: the float spelling of an integer never becomes the integer, so the plainest spelling of that cell's mutant survives — a mutant-less cell inside the very sentence asserting none exists.

The coordinator declined to pass-with-notes for a reason worth keeping: the package states at its head that it deliberately carries no corrections appendix, because a package whose corrections live in a separate section is read inconsistently — so corrections living only in a verdict document would have been exactly the shape it forbids.

ALL FOUR ARE NOW CLOSED IN THE PACKAGE ITSELF, by the orchestrator, each verified at the source first: the grep is scoped to the interface-specification file with the reason written beside it and the product-requirements line added to the do-not-edit list; the mutation range is corrected with an explicit note naming the two mutants the old range would have skipped and why that mattered; the cell's mutant is re-specified to the spelling that actually kills it, with the retired spelling quoted and forbidden so nobody restores it; and the dangling section reference is fixed. Verified by grep that no residual carries the retired forms except the two deliberate do-not-restore quotations.

IMPLEMENT IN FLIGHT: a single implementer in an isolated worktree off main, branch ubcnv-envelope-id-reject, landing the spec commit first (the new decision row, the reciprocal note, the interface and threat-model corrections, the crate plan, both roadmaps, and the decision-range bump at every enumerated site including the shipped scripts' knobs) and then the implementation commits. It must reproduce the defect on raw bytes in its own worktree BEFORE the fix and re-run the same frames after, and run the full local gate rather than a subset. The mutation matrix is deliberately NOT its job: an adversarial Verify gate measures it next, because self-measured coverage is exactly what this repo has learned not to trust.

Two Track-step duties are already recorded so they cannot be discovered late: the git record .unblock/issues.jsonl must be re-exported in this same pull request so ub-788 exists in it — the decision row names that id, and without the export the product-requirements document would ship a dangling reference — and the wiki run-report lands in the same commit.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Implement outcome (2026-08-06). Branch ubcnv-envelope-id-reject, six atomic commits off main. The Verify gate is now in flight.

IT TOOK TWO RUNS. The first implementer was killed by a session limit after landing four commits, mid-way through the last piece of work. Nothing was lost: it had been told to commit incrementally precisely so an interruption would be survivable, and the worktree kept its history. A continuation was launched into the SAME worktree — not a fresh one, and not a restart — and it verified what was already committed before adding anything, rather than redoing it.

THE COMMITS, in order: the spec commit minting the decision and its whole cascade; the transport change answering an un-decodable envelope id and dropping the frame; the byte-identity pin rebuilt in three tiers for the new arm; the test commit covering the class over a live duplex, real stdio and the pre-handshake position; the required-landing gate for this decision with its continuous-integration step; and the tracker re-export.

PROVEN ON THE WIRE, before and after, against the two binaries rather than by reading. Post-handshake, every in-class frame was SILENT on main and is now answered: the same id twice comes back with the invalid-request error carrying THAT id; two different ids, a null id and the exponent spelling of an integer each come back with the id omitted; a repeated string id answers on the string. The frame with NO id gets NO response on BOTH binaries — the notification rule holds and the fix is targeted rather than blanket, which was the single most important negative in the whole plan. A clean request afterwards is answered normally, so the connection is not desynchronised. And in the pre-handshake position the same frame went from killing the process — exit code 1, with a non-JSON-RPC blob written onto the framing channel — to being answered, after which a full handshake and a subsequent request succeed on that same connection, exiting 0. The no-id notification pre-handshake still exits 1 with the blob, correctly, because that is the separate defect tracked as ub-og3.

THE GATE, run in the implementer's own worktree with its own build directory: formatting, pedantic clippy across the workspace, the whole suite at 1701 tests, snapshots, the documentation lint over its nineteen documents, the knowledge lint over sixty pages, the layering check, and every claims-check script — all green.

ONE BLOCKER, AND IT WAS A PACKAGE DEFECT RATHER THAN A CODE ONE — reported instead of worked around, which is the behaviour this repo asks for. The new gate requires the residual issue ub-788 to be present in the committed git record. The package assigns that re-export to the TRACK step, which runs after both gates, while minting the script itself in the implementation commit — so the required check was red by construction until Track ran. The implementer explicitly refused to weaken the assertion to make it pass, and could not discharge it either: it has no tracker tools, no command-line verb creates issues, the live database lives in the checkout it is forbidden to touch, and hand-editing the generated export is what the export model forbids. The orchestrator discharged it: exported the record over the tracker tool, copied it onto the branch, RESTORED the shared checkout to its exact prior state (verified by checksum), and committed it. The gate now passes. The sequencing defect itself is worth remembering — a required check whose rows pin landings from a LATER step than the commit that mints it is red by construction.

A FINDING REPORTED RATHER THAN SWEPT, and it is not ours: one intermittent failure appeared in a storage stress test for parallel first writes, with a backend API-misuse error; it passed five of five on isolated re-runs and the full suite was green afterwards. It is unrelated to this branch, which touches no crate below the top layer. Filed as ub-q1u with the caution written into it that the tempting diagnosis — "it is just the test" — is the one that must be proved rather than assumed, because this failure surfaces from the library on the very contention path the concurrency requirement exists to protect.

VERIFY GATE IN FLIGHT: four lenses, each in its own isolated worktree, plus a coordinator. One MEASURES the mutation matrix — deliberately withheld from the implementer, because self-measured coverage is exactly what this repo has learned not to trust — prioritising the fail-open mutants, the three uniqueness claims, and the mutant that fails only on a raw-span value comparator. One attacks the shipped binary over raw bytes hunting a frame that still hangs, a false positive on legitimate notification traffic, an answer carrying the wrong id, and any regression in the neighbouring duplicate-key defence. One reviews the diff as shipped code and judges every normative sentence landed against what the code actually does. One re-runs every gate independently and judges whether the rebuilt byte-identity test still catches a dependency bump or has been hollowed into passing by construction. The wiki run-report and any final re-export are named as Track-owned and pending, so the gate reports them rather than failing the change for their absence.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Verify gate + Track (2026-08-06). Verify = PASS WITH MUST-FIXES, fix pass, re-verify = PASS. Twelve atomic commits on ubcnv-envelope-id-reject, pushed. The pull request is NOT yet open — the command-line tool is unauthenticated in this environment and Miguel needs to authorise it; everything else is done.

THE MECHANISM SURVIVED EVERYTHING. Twenty-six of twenty-six catalogue mutants killed with zero survivors, plus about thirty further mutants across two more lenses with disjoint harnesses and no non-equivalent survivor anywhere. The defect is closed by EFFECT rather than by reading: six frames of the class carrying issue-creating payloads were each answered and the listing afterwards came back empty. The frame with no id is byte-identical on both binaries across nine shapes, so the fix is targeted rather than blanket. And the pre-handshake case went from killing the process to being answered, after which a full handshake and a further request succeed on that same connection.

THE FOUR MUST-FIXES, none of which touched the mechanism. A permission bit: the new gate script was committed non-executable while all four siblings are executable, and the continuous-integration job invokes them as bare paths with no interpreter — it would have died on its first run, and every local check had passed because they were being run through an explicit shell, which masks exactly that. Two rows of that same new gate were satisfiable by a doc comment: the pattern also matched a comment and a test body, so the production line could be reverted and the gate would still have reported the arm present — a false coverage claim inside the very check that exists to prevent them, now re-anchored on production lines and proven by applying each mutant. A crate plan promising tests that did not exist, where Miguel ruled to LAND THE TESTS rather than soften the plan. And the concurrency residual below.

THE RESIDUAL MIGUEL RULED ON. The reply is lost whenever the dependency cancels our read future under concurrent traffic, because the reply is written inside that future — measured at none lost on an idle connection, twenty-five of forty with four requests in flight, thirty-nine of forty with eight. It is PRE-EXISTING: the parse-error arm already shipped in the release behaves identically, which is what makes it a property of the transport rather than of this change. The severe case this task exists to remove happens by definition with nothing in flight, the regime measured at zero losses. Ruling: disclose and track, fix as its own task — now ub-nbz, with its acceptance criteria written to require the rates be REPLICATED, since they come from one harness and are recorded as such.

TWO THINGS THE TEAM REFUSED TO CLAIM, and both are the behaviour this repo wants. The gate asked for eight visitor arms to be graded, on the premise that a missing test cell would do it; the premise was FALSE — deleting those arms and keeping them both reach the same verdict by different routes, so no corpus of bytes can distinguish them. The fixer proved it an equivalent mutant and wrote the limit into the test's own documentation instead of claiming a kill. Separately, a commit message asserted that one cell fails ALONE under a given mutant; a sibling cell splices the same boundary value with the real decoder as its oracle, so both must fail together. Miguel ruled to rewrite the message rather than let a false coverage claim become permanent record — the branch was unmerged, so it was safe then and impossible after a merge. The rewrite is content-neutral: the tree is byte-identical before and after.

TRACK LANDED: the placeholder for the residual id substituted at both sites with zero survivors; the disclosure cascade closed at both roadmap cards, where Miguel chose to STRIKE the count word rather than change three to four, because the standing rule is that the list is the rule and carries no count — and a derived count has already rotted at that exact site five times; a required-landing row added so the newly-named id cannot become the dangling reference its sibling row exists to prevent; the transport's disclosure aligned with the decision row's measured figures including the unreplicated caveat; the git record re-exported; and the run-report written with its mandatory glossary.

FULL GATE GREEN, re-run at the final tip: formatting, pedantic lints, 1703 tests, the snapshot check (the one hole nobody had covered since the fix pass — clean), the documentation lint, the knowledge lint over sixty-one pages, the layering check, all five claims scripts invoked the way the continuous-integration job invokes them, and the run-report gate with its self-test.

FOUR ISSUES OPENED FROM THIS WORK, each with acceptance criteria written to block the easy answer: ub-og3 for the non-JSON-RPC blob written onto the framing channel at startup failure; ub-788 for the parse-error arm that swallows a readable id, blocked on this one; ub-q1u for an intermittent storage stress failure seen during the gate and unrelated to this branch; and ub-nbz as above.

TWO GOTCHAS FOR THE NEXT SESSION, both in the run-report: a required check whose rows pin landings from a LATER lifecycle step than the commit that mints it is red by construction — this gate demanded a tracking-step export from an implementation commit; and a claims script committed without its executable bit passes every local invocation through a shell and dies in continuous integration, which runs it as a bare path.

Remaining: Miguel authorises the command-line tool, the pull request opens, a human merges, and this issue closes on that merge.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Pull request opened: PR 438 (branch ubcnv-envelope-id-reject into main) — https://github.com/websublime/unblock/pull/438. Twelve atomic commits, twenty-nine files, 2975 insertions against 140 deletions.

The body carries the reproduction before and after on raw bytes, the real class of the defect (an un-decodable id, of which duplication is the minority route), the full gate history, the four residuals with their issue ids, and two items flagged for Miguel's eye at merge: the equivalent mutant the team declared instead of faking a kill, and the commit message rewritten because it carried a false coverage claim.

On the tooling: the command-line client had no stored credential and its login is interactive, so this was blocked briefly; Miguel pointed at a workspace token in the environment and the pull request opened with it. Recording that here because the same wall will be hit by any future session that assumes the client is authenticated.

Claude does not merge. On merge, close this task.

description:
Found 2026-07-27 by the ub-lp9.21 Spec/Plan probe, which was verifying a DIFFERENT claim and turned this up as a by-product. Miguel scoped it OUT of the ub-lp9.21 fix and into its own issue, in the same v1.0.1 patch slot, so it gets a proper diagnosis instead of widening a PR that is already large.

OBSERVATION: a JSON-RPC frame carrying a DUPLICATE `id` member in the envelope is not decoded as the request it reads as. The duplicate collapses and the frame degrades to a shape the server treats as a NOTIFICATION, so NO response is emitted at all and a client waiting on that id hangs indefinitely. This is a distinct defect from ub-lp9.21's discriminant flip: there the wrong action executes, here nothing answers.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FOLDED INTO ub-lp9.21: it cannot be reported through the in-band structured-error channel, because there is no usable request id to answer on — any rejection is necessarily an out-of-band protocol fault. Miguel's binding decision for ub-lp9.21 was in-band rejection, so covering this there would have contradicted it.

ALSO CORRECTED HERE, because the record was wrong: the earlier ub-lp9.21 analysis stated that the JSON-RPC envelope is immune to duplicate keys BECAUSE its typed struct fields receive serde's duplicate-field detection. The probe established that this mechanism claim is WRONG. Envelope duplicates are not rejected by duplicate-field detection; they degrade to an unknown-request shape answered with a method-not-found protocol error — and, in the `id` case, to no answer at all. The observable outcome for `method`/`name` is still a rejection, so the ub-lp9.21 blast-radius conclusion is unaffected, but the reason differs and this issue is the part that is genuinely open.

INVESTIGATE FIRST, then decide the fix. Do not assume the duplicate is the only path to the notification reinterpretation — establish what the decoder actually does, and whether other envelope members degrade the same way.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The behaviour is reproduced live over raw JSON-RPC stdio bytes and documented: what is sent, what the server decodes it as, and what (if anything) the client receives.
- Established whether members other than `id` produce the same silent-notification degradation.
- A decision is recorded on the response: reject the frame as a protocol fault, or accept the degradation as conforming behaviour with an explicit rationale. If rejected, the channel is necessarily out-of-band and the spine's in-band argument-boundary promise must be reconciled to say so.
- Regression coverage at the raw-bytes wire level; note that the existing test harness serializes a value object and is structurally incapable of expressing a duplicate member, so the ub-lp9.21 raw-bytes capability is a prerequisite.
- No frame can leave a conforming client waiting with no response and no diagnostic.
title: Bug: a duplicate envelope `id` reinterprets a request as a notification — the client gets no response and hangs

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text: Widened at the ub-kp7 Verify gate (2026-09-14): a second unblock-storage cell failed once inside a full workspace run under load and passed three of three in isolation, in the same session and on the same byte-unchanged crate. It is write_lock_flock_contention_and_fairness in crates/unblock-storage/tests/contention_lab.rs. Whatever remedy is chosen for the non-vacuity control in write_lock_two_process.rs must cover this cell too, so fixing the first does not leave the second to redden the required test job.

description:
Observed 2026-09-14 by the ub-kp7 (D50) orchestrator while running cargo test --workspace --all-features on the branch ub-kp7-pre-initialize-gate, with four Verify-gate worktrees compiling in parallel (load average above 12). Reported rather than swept: the branch touches nothing under crates/unblock-storage.

SYMPTOM. crates/unblock-storage/tests/write_lock_two_process.rs, cell cross_process_write_lock_prevents_id_collision, failed at :133 with "the no-lock control must REPRODUCE the IdCollision (got 0 — the test would be vacuous)". The locked half of the cell passed; the NON-VACUITY CONTROL failed, because under that load the two child processes racing WITHOUT the D31 .write.lock never overlapped, so no IdCollision occurred and the control read as vacuous. Re-run three times in isolation immediately afterwards: 3 of 3 green, each under one second.

WHY IT MATTERS. The control exists so the locked assertion cannot pass vacuously, which is the right discipline, but a control that depends on two processes actually colliding is timing-dependent by construction: a loaded runner serialises them and the control fails for a reason unrelated to the lock. On the required test job this reads as a storage regression.

REMEDY, to decide rather than assume. Either make the collision deterministic (a rendezvous so both children reach the allocation read before either writes, for example a barrier file or a shared pipe each child waits on), or retry the no-lock control a bounded number of times before declaring vacuity, or move the control to a separate cell marked as load-sensitive. Whichever is chosen, the locked assertion must keep its non-vacuity guarantee. Sibling flake record: ub-q1u (libsql open_in_memory_parallel_first_write_stress).
title: Flaky: write_lock_two_process non-vacuity control fails under load (the no-lock race never collides)

description:
Found by the ub-kp7 (D50) Implement phase on 2026-09-14 and split out rather than absorbed, because D50 limits its edits to shipped sibling gates to the ub-kp7 reason strings.

WHAT IT IS. scripts/checks/d49-startup-failure-render-claims.sh carries two self-wiring landings as bare-token PRESENCE rows: the row over .github/workflows/ci.yml (the gate actually runs in the required doc-lint job) and the row over docs/PROCESS.md (the section 3 list names the script). A presence row is satisfied by ANY line containing the token, so a workflow step commented out with the script name left in the comment, or a PROCESS.md sentence that mentions the script without listing it, keeps both rows green while the landing is gone.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. While building the D50 sibling (scripts/checks/d50-pre-handshake-gate-claims.sh), the same two rows were written as presence rows first, and a mutation pass proved both survive: commenting the workflow step out and dropping the PROCESS.md list entry left the script green. The D50 script re-anchored them as ROW-ANCHORED rows (the workflow row anchored on the run step itself, the PROCESS row anchored on the list entry carrying both knob names), and the same two mutations then turned it red. The D49 sibling was left as shipped.

REMEDY. Re-anchor the two D49 rows the way the D50 script does (anchor on the run step line and on the list entry), verify by the same two mutations, and check whether the D44, D45 (ub-lp9.25), D46, D47 and D48 siblings carry the same shape of row, since the header of each says every sibling carries the self-wiring rows. Positive-only discipline applies: no negative sweep for a commented-out spelling.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Orchestrator orientation (2026-08-07), off main at 9adc2cb.

State established before touching anything:

The codebase graph is ALREADY indexed and fresh — index_status reports ready, 7367 nodes / 35275 edges, at head_sha 9adc2cb which is the current main tip. The fourth bullet of this issue ("actually index the repository") is therefore already satisfied and produces no artifact to commit.

Neither CLAUDE.md nor docs/PROCESS.md belongs to the doc-lint corpus (the fixed nineteen-file list in xtask/src/doc_lint.rs), so neither edit can trip that lint. No D-id is minted, so the decision-range cascade over the required check scripts is not triggered.

The run-report gate WILL classify this pull request as substantive, because .mcp.json is an always-substantive path in the predicate. A wiki run-report of at least ten added lines is therefore due in the same pull request, written by the Track step, not by Implement.

Miguel's fork resolutions this session:
- The codebase-memory server entry in .mcp.json IS committed as part of this task. He was told the trade-off explicitly — the binary lives outside this public repo, so a fresh clone gets a server that fails to start — and chose to commit it without adding an install note to AGENTS.md.
- The full lifecycle applies: design Review gate, then a spawned Implement team writing in an isolated worktree, then the Verify gate, then Track.
- The stale-closed-state lag found below gets no follow-up issue; the re-export corrects it in place.
- The .mcp.json entry that starts this server itself is NOT touched in this pull request.

Two defects found while orienting, both worth recording:

First, the unblock MCP server did not connect to this session. The server is healthy — a direct stdio handshake answers in milliseconds on contract unblock.mcp.v1.9. The cause is the wiring: .mcp.json starts it with `cargo run`, whose cold build far exceeds the MCP client's startup timeout (the debug binary was rebuilt at the exact minute this session started; warm, the same command answers in two seconds). A long-lived server process from a concurrent session started the previous day is also still alive on this checkout. Work proceeds through a stdio harness against the already-built binary.

Second, the committed git record was stale. A re-export changed exactly one record: this issue's predecessor ub-og3 was still recorded as in_progress, with no closed_at and no close_reason, while the store has it closed at 2026-08-07T09:07:40Z referencing its merged pull request. The cause is ordering, not corruption: the record was exported at 09:06Z and the issue closed at 09:07:40Z — the export ran a minute before the close. This is structural rather than accidental, since the process mandates exporting in the work commit but closing on merge, which is always later; the closed state therefore reaches the git record one pull request late. The re-export done here corrects it and rides this task's commit.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design Review gate (2026-08-07) — verdict: PASS WITH CHANGES.

Recorded late: the gate ran in the previous session, which ended before its outcome reached this thread. The verdict and the byte-exact spec it produced were recovered from that session's working files and are restated here in full, so the thread is the record rather than a pointer to a lost transcript.

Shape of the pass: three adversarial lenses — architecture (doc hierarchy and rule placement), evidence (does the claimed hook text and tooling actually exist and say what the issue says), operability (can a team execute the instruction as written) — plus a coordinator. The consolidated output superseded the design brief's proposed wording in full and became a verbatim implementation spec, so the implementer made no judgement calls.

Substantive rulings, each of which changed the wording that was about to be written:

The rule is EXTENDED in place, on the existing hard-rules bullet about semantic search, rather than minted as a sixth bullet. The list stays at five bullets. A second rule about the same subject in a second document is exactly how these decay, which is the argument the issue itself makes.

The phrase "discovery, not authority" must stay contiguous on that line. An acceptance criterion at docs/plans/implementation-plan.md:77 cites the rule by that phrase, and that file IS in the doc-lint corpus; breaking the phrase would have forced an edit there and pulled a corpus file into a pull request that otherwise cannot trip the lint at all.

The literal D-range spelling used across the decision cascade must not appear anywhere in the new text. scripts/checks/d44-create-deps-claims.sh rests a file-level check on CLAUDE.md carrying exactly one occurrence of that literal; a second one turns a required job red for a reason unrelated to its own decision.

The enumeration of structural questions (who calls this, is this reachable, which paths do X, what does this depend on) lives in exactly ONE place — the CLAUDE.md bullet. PROCESS.md carries mechanics only and repeats no list. Two copies of one list is the rot class the process guide legislates against by name.

The sentence in PROCESS.md section 4 licensing Explore for broad search is scoped to broad TEXT search. Unamended it was the only other statement in either always-in-context file about how an Understand team searches, and as written it licensed precisely the grep-first behaviour this task exists to stop.

The Understand comment on a task's issue gains one field — graph: used, stale at a named sha, or unavailable with a reason — kept on one physical line so that a single grep over the committed record audits compliance across every task.

Explicitly out of scope, and none of it was touched: no decision id, no PRD row, no roadmap, spine or crate-plan edit, no live-range knob in any check script, no entry in the CLAUDE.md document map (the graph is not a normative doc and must hold no rank in the PRD over spine over crate-plans hierarchy), no writes under .knowledge by the implementer, and .mcp.json committed exactly as Miguel decided it, unmodified.

One disclosure the gate insisted on, because it changes what this change buys today: the rule is currently INERT for spawned teams, by the tooling's design and not by the text's. All twelve agent definitions under .claude/agents declare an explicit tools allow-list, and not one of them lists any MCP tool; .claude/settings.json grants no MCP permission either. So every spawned Understand or Verify team lands in the "unavailable" arm until a follow-up grants the tools — which is what that arm exists for, reporting the gap instead of silently grepping around it. The actor whose omission opened this task, the main-session orchestrator, does have the tools. The follow-up that grants them is filed separately and is deliberately NOT in this pull request, since .claude is itself an always-substantive path and would drag a second run-report obligation into it.

comments.text:
Implement phase — done, uncommitted, awaiting the Verify gate.

A single implementer agent wrote in an isolated worktree (the artifact had to stay coherent: two prose edits whose wording is load-bearing against each other). Its patch was assembled into the task worktree at .claude/worktrees/ub-gwe, on branch ub-gwe-code-graph-first, based on main at 9adc2cb. Nothing is committed yet — the branch carries no commits and the change lives as working-tree modifications, which is where the Verify gate picks it up.

What the change is, in four files' worth of effect but two edited files:

CLAUDE.md, the hard-rules bullet that used to speak only about semantic search, is replaced by one that draws the boundary both ways. A structural question goes to the code-graph MCP tools before any grep sweep, pointing at PROCESS.md section 4 for the server and phase mechanics; a text question — a zero-live-hits sweep, doc or config content, a literal string — stays grep's. If the graph is unavailable, unindexed, or indexed at another commit, the duty is to fix it or say so in the task's issue comment, never to fall back silently. The authority cap the old bullet carried survives verbatim: the graph and semantic search locate file and line, and never replace a full read of the authoritative spec or of the original source when exact fidelity matters.

docs/PROCESS.md section 4 gets two hunks. The Explore sentence is scoped to broad TEXT search. Below it, a new paragraph states that Understand opens at the code graph, points back at the CLAUDE.md rule for the boundary and the never-silently-fall-back duty rather than restating either, names the server and the fact that its index is machine-local and commit-stamped (so it is the MAIN checkout that gets indexed, never a throwaway worktree), and adds the one-line field the Understand comment now carries.

Riding the same change set, both already decided: the codebase-memory entry in .mcp.json, committed exactly as it stands, and the .unblock/issues.jsonl re-export.

Conformance to the reviewed spec was re-checked mechanically rather than by eye, and all of it holds: the CLAUDE.md bullet is ONE physical line of 850 characters (its neighbours are unwrapped lines too, so wrapping it would have been the anomaly); the phrase "discovery, not authority" occurs contiguously and exactly once; the file contains zero middot characters, which are a PROCESS.md idiom and not a CLAUDE.md one; the decision-range literal still occurs exactly once, so the check script that rests on that count is untouched; the closing sentence about a returned chunk being a pointer survives verbatim; the hard-rules list is still five bullets; no trailing whitespace was introduced in either file; and every added PROCESS.md line is at or under 110 columns, matching that file's wrap.

Known pending and NOT a Verify failure, per the process guide's ownership rule: the .knowledge run-report and the final record re-export belong to the Track step, after the gate.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Verify quality gate (2026-08-07), round one — verdict: PASS WITH NOTES. Zero must-fixes. Three cheap prose hardenings proposed, none blocking the commit.

Shape: three adversarial lenses plus a coordinator, each lens in its OWN private checkout with the change applied, so no lens could clobber another and none could touch the shared tree. Lenses: a claim audit (does the new prose assert more than is true), an executable-gates lens (run everything that could go red), and a coupling lens (break each claimed coupling and observe what actually turns red). The coordinator held a read-only assignment and re-checked the load-bearing facts at source rather than trusting the lens reports.

WHAT WAS PROVEN GREEN, by execution rather than by reading. No landed byte is wrong and no required job goes red because of this change. The doc-lint corpus is a fixed nineteen-file list and excludes both edited documents — counted at source, and proven non-vacuous by a positive control that injected rejectable bytes into a corpus file and got two findings back. CLAUDE.md still carries exactly one live decision-range literal, at the document-map row, untouched by an edit that lands twenty lines below it. The phrase-contiguity coupling to the acceptance criterion in the implementation plan is intact.

THREE FINDINGS THAT ARE WORTH THE ISSUE THREAD RATHER THAN A PULL-REQUEST FOOTNOTE.

First, a design-gate claim is CORRECTED. The design gate said a required check rests on CLAUDE.md containing exactly ONE occurrence of the live decision-range literal. Mutation proved that wording is a rationale comment, not an enforced assertion: appending a second occurrence left that script and all four sibling range scripts green, while changing the literal to a stale range did fire the row check red. So only PRESENCE is enforced. Nothing is broken today, and this change adds no second occurrence — but a FUTURE decision cascade that adds a second live-range mention to CLAUDE.md would silently defeat the rationale that justifies not row-anchoring that site.

Second, the rewritten hard rule is protected by CONVENTION ONLY. Deleting the entire bullet outright leaves all six check scripts green and the doc-lint reporting clean; breaking the phrase contiguity is equally invisible. The same probe caught injected bytes in a corpus file, so the probe was not vacuous — the rule simply has no executable guard. The acceptance criterion in the implementation plan that restates it is coupled to CLAUDE.md by prose alone.

Third, a required-job script is RED AT BASELINE and unrelated to this change: scripts/knowledge/tests/landing-verify.sh fails with byte-identical four-failure output on pristine main and with the change applied, measured independently by two lenses in separate checkouts. It is wired into no workflow — the doc-lint job runs the six check scripts plus doc-lint, knowledge-lint and the run-report-gate selftest, and never calls it. It must not block this pull request and it deserves its own issue.

THE THREE PROSE HARDENINGS, each one clause, all in the new bytes. The rule prescribes duties the docs give no means to perform: it says index or re-index the main checkout, and it says fix it or say so, without naming a single command or tool verb anywhere — and a repo-wide grep finds the server named ONLY in .mcp.json and the two edited files, with the tool's own description living outside this public repository. A rule whose remedy is unnamed collapses into its escape hatch. Next, nothing tells a future session that reporting the graph as stale during BRANCH work, and naming what answered instead, is the CORRECT outcome rather than a process violation — the index tracks the main checkout while every Implement team writes in an isolated worktree, so that case is the norm, not the exception. Last, the placeholder for the stale value in the new issue-comment field invites a token that the run-report gate's session-local-id predicate matches, if a sha is ever hand-written with a leading uppercase hex letter; spelling the placeholder as a lowercase short sha closes it.

KNOWN-PENDING, and explicitly NOT a gate failure per the process guide's ownership rule: the .knowledge run-report and a fresh record re-export belong to the Track step. Measured consequence, so nobody is surprised later — the run-report gate exits non-zero on this change set with "always-substantive path: .mcp.json", and the pull-request-creation hook blocks accordingly. Also measured: the two doc edits ALONE would classify as trivial (a ten-line docs delta under the twenty-line budget). The .mcp.json entry is the sole substantive trigger; anyone reasoning that the docs edit forces the run-report has the wrong file.

Two smaller notes carried forward rather than acted on. The rewritten bullet grew from 356 to 850 characters in a file whose own guidance is pointers over prose, and the next-longest line there is 264 — the design gate approved the bytes, and the cost is named rather than hidden. And CLAUDE.md names .mcp.json together with AGENTS.md as where the MCP wiring and tool surface live, while AGENTS.md still describes only the unblock server; not false, since that file is scoped by its own heading, but it now under-reports if it is meant to be the agent-facing wiring index.
