comments.text:
Track — shipped to review. Pull request 440 on branch ub-gwe-code-graph-first, off main at 9adc2cb. The issue stays in_progress; it closes on merge, which is a human gate.

THREE ATOMIC COMMITS, in the order a reviewer should read them.

The first carries the two prose edits together, because they are one logical change split across the contract and the process guide by the rule that the boundary lives in the contract and the mechanics in the guide. The second commits the codebase-memory entry in .mcp.json, with the trade-off Miguel accepted written into the message rather than left implicit, and pointing at the two issues that track its consequences. The third is the Track step's own: the record re-export and the wiki run-report, landing on top of the gated commits so they ride the same pull request, which is exactly what the ownership rule prescribes.

THE THREE HARDENINGS the Verify gate proposed were all applied, on Miguel's decision, by a second single implementer in an isolated worktree — all three inside the process-guide paragraph, so the contract file came out byte-identical to the version the design gate fixed, proven by an md5 of the diff hunk rather than by eye. The paragraph now names the two tool verbs, states that declaring the graph stale during branch work and naming what answered instead is the correct outcome there, and asks the stale placeholder for a lowercase short sha.

DELTA RE-VERIFICATION, run because the Verify coordinator said in writing that its verdict covered only the bytes it graded and not any later difference: six check scripts all exit 0; doc-lint OK across nineteen documents; knowledge-lint OK across sixty-three pages; layering OK; the run-report gate now passes on the branch, reporting the always-substantive path and finding the report that satisfies it. Plus the mechanical property set the design spec fixed — one physical line of 845 characters, the phrase contiguous exactly once, zero middot characters, the decision-range literal still occurring exactly once, five bullets, the closing sentence verbatim, no trailing whitespace, and the eight added guide lines peaking at 107 characters. The three field values were tested against the predicate regular expression and none matches, while a sha hand-written with a leading uppercase hexadecimal letter does — so the third hardening closed a real hole rather than a hypothetical one.

TWO SMALL CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER COMMENTS IN THIS THREAD, so the record is not left overstating itself. The Implement summary above says the rewritten bullet is 850 characters; that figure was measured in BYTES. In characters it is 845, and the difference is the multi-byte em-dashes. Separately, the Verify comment relayed the gate's claim that the AGENTS.md wiring row under-reports the new server; while filing that finding it turned out the contract's document-map row is scoped to the unblock tracker by its own heading, so it is accurate as written. The real and narrower defect — that the repository has nowhere at all to describe a second MCP server — is what ub-amw records.

FIVE FINDINGS FILED rather than absorbed, all open: ub-4ne, ub-wvh, ub-lg7, ub-tge, ub-amw. The first is the one a reviewer should read before approving, because it bounds what this change buys today: no spawned agent team can reach the graph tools at all, and the entry being committed is project-scoped and therefore inert until approved, so it reads as wired without starting.

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE TEAM LINEUP, disclosed rather than quietly taken. The Track agent was spawned with an agent type whose tool allow-list has no write tool, so it could not create the run-report file and the knowledge-tree shell guard blocked every fallback; it returned the finished text and the orchestrator materialised the bytes after checking them against the template and the sibling report. The commits and the pull request were made by the orchestrator directly. Both are recorded in the run-report's gotchas, together with the lesson: pick the agent type by the tools the artifact needs, not by the subject matter.

description:
Raised by Miguel on 2026-08-07, from evidence in the ub-og3 session.

WHAT HAPPENED. A SessionStart hook instructs every session to reach for the codebase-graph MCP tools FIRST for any code exploration. Across the whole ub-og3 task the orchestrator never called them once, and never said so — it went straight to Read, Grep and shell greps, and delegated the rest to subagents using their own tools. When Miguel asked directly, a check showed the server also had ZERO projects indexed, so the tools were not usable without an index_repository call that nobody made. Two failures, not one: the protocol was ignored, and the fact that it could not be followed as written was never surfaced.

WHY IT COST SOMETHING, concretely. The ub-og3 Understand phase asked exactly the questions a code graph answers: every path that can write to file descriptor 1 on one command, whether `Session::open` is reachable, how many callers `into_exit` has, which shipped tests assert a given payload. Those were answered with grep sweeps across several agent rounds. One of them — that `into_exit` has exactly ONE caller — turned out to be load-bearing enough that the D48 gate script now has to pin it, because a second caller passing the wrong argument would silently re-open the defect.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY "USE THE TOOL MORE". CLAUDE.md already carries a hard rule that semantic search is DISCOVERY, NOT AUTHORITY: it locates file:line, and never replaces a full read of the authoritative spec or of the original source when exact fidelity matters. That rule is correct and must survive intact — most of ub-og3 was spec and measurement work where a graph would have added nothing. The gap is the missing POSITIVE half: nothing says the graph is the FIRST move for a structural question, and nothing says what to do when the repository is not indexed.

SCOPE — two edits, deliberately small, in the two always-in-context files:
1. CLAUDE.md — extend the existing semantic-search hard rule to cover the code graph explicitly, rather than minting a competing rule in another file. A second rule about the same thing in a different document is how these decay.
2. docs/PROCESS.md section 4 — in the Understand phase, state that structural questions (who calls this, is this reachable, what are all the paths that do X, what does this depend on) go to the graph FIRST, and that an unindexed repository is either indexed or reported — never silently worked around.

NOT a D-id: this is methodology, not a product or interface decision, so it belongs in PROCESS.md and CLAUDE.md and not in PRD section 4. No D-range bump.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUNDLED into the ub-og3 / D48 pull request: unrelated subject matter, and the repo requires atomic commits and one pull request per task.

ALSO PENDING and part of this: actually index the repository, so the next session's first call is a query rather than an index. The `.mcp.json` entry wiring the server was already present, uncommitted, in the working tree at the start of the ub-og3 session; decide whether it should be committed as part of this.
title: Chore: make the codebase graph a stated first move for structural questions — CLAUDE.md rule + PROCESS.md Understand-phase instruction

description:
Surfaced 2026-09-21 by the ub-w3a research spike, verified directly against the vendored crate at
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/libsql-0.9.30 rather than taken from a lens report.

THE TRAP. The libsql crate gates three different connection shapes behind three different cargo
features, and the one we named ours after is the wrong one.

  feature "replication" gates Builder::new_remote_replica(path, url, auth_token) at
  src/database/builder.rs:52, inside a cfg_replication! block, documented as "Create a new remote
  embedded replica". This is the embedded replica, a local database file kept in step with a primary.
  It is the shape v1.3 specifies, where reads stay local and writes go to the primary.

  feature "remote" gates Builder::new_remote(url, auth_token) at src/database/builder.rs:128, inside a
  cfg_remote! block, documented as "Create a new remote database". It takes NO path. There is no local
  file and no local read. Every query crosses the network over the Hrana protocol.

  feature "sync" gates Builder::new_synced_database(path, url, auth_token) at
  src/database/builder.rs:98, documented as "Create a database that can be written offline and synced
  to a remote server". It pulls in both remote and replication.

WHAT WE WROTE. crates/unblock-storage/Cargo.toml declares an empty marker feature named "remote", and
unblock-engine forwards remote = ["unblock-storage/remote"]. docs/plans/crates/unblock-storage.md:36
places BOTH LibsqlStorage::open_remote(...) and open_replica(...) behind feature = "remote", and
line 82 gives src/libsql/remote.rs the same gate while describing its content as "embedded-replica
local-read + remote-write-back".

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NAMING NIT. The marker feature is empty today, so the moment it
stops being empty someone has to write what it forwards to. The obvious reading of the plan is
remote = ["libsql/remote"], and that resolves to the pathless network-per-query client. The failure is
silent at the type level, since both constructors yield a Database and the Storage trait cannot tell
them apart. It would surface as every read crossing the network, which contradicts the local-read half
of the v1.3 contract in docs/plans/00-roadmap.md section 4 and the standing rule that no normal command
path touches the network.

The transitive cost differs too, which matters for keeping the default build free of TLS and HTTP.
"remote" pulls hrana, hyper, http, tower and base64. "replication" pulls tonic, tonic-web, tower-http,
libsql_replication, bincode, zerocopy and uuid. They are not interchangeable dependency sets, so any
budget reasoning done against one does not transfer to the other.

WHAT TO FIX, AND WHEN. Not now. The correct mapping depends on which direction the v1.3 lock takes,
because the turso crate's sync path does not use any of these three. Resolve this AT the v1.3 lock, in
the same change that settles the mechanism, by naming the cargo feature after the shape it actually
gates and correcting the two crate-plan lines and the spine's remote constructor signatures together.

Parent context: ub-w3a. Do not close this independently of that lock.
title: Finding: the storage cargo feature named remote maps to the wrong libsql constructor, which would put every read on the network

description: Pre-existing, intermittent CI flake, unrelated to any current feature work — surfaced (not caused) by PR #429's CI run. In crates/unblock-model/tests/proptest_model_roundtrip.rs the strategies arb_issue_type() and arb_status() include a Custom arm generated from "[a-zA-Z]{1,12}", which can (rarely) produce a string equal to a CANONICAL variant name (issue_type: Task/Bug/Epic; status: Open/InProgress/Blocked/Closed). serde serializes Custom("Bug") to the wire string "Bug" and deserializes "Bug" back to the canonical IssueType::Bug, so the round-trip is NOT identity for those colliding strings and the prop_assert_eq!(left, right) fails. Observed on PR #429: issue_type_roundtrip failed with left=Custom("Bug") right=Bug after 97 successes (proptest saved regression cc 86c50f4d...). status_roundtrip carries the same latent defect (passed by luck this run). The model normalization (Custom("Bug") == Bug on the wire) is arguably correct; the DEFECT is in the test generator, which must exclude the canonical variant names from the Custom arm (e.g. prop_filter rejecting the known names, or a charset/shape disjoint from them). Fix lives entirely in the unblock-model test file; a plain `gh run rerun --failed` unblocks any PR that trips it meanwhile (rare seed). Acceptance: the Custom arms cannot generate a canonical variant name; the roundtrip proptests are deterministic-green across repeated runs (bump proptest cases locally to confirm).
title: proptest roundtrip generators emit Custom(canonical-name) → intermittent CI flake in unblock-model

comments.text: Decide-phase record (2026-07-21, main-session conversation with Miguel). Trigger: Miguel flagged a v1.0.1 Verify-gate report as cryptic — it used session-local codes (a mutant id "M10", a must-fix id "MF-2", briefing rules "R7/R8", "lens 3/4", a "facet (b)" label) that cannot be resolved outside the originating session; a grep over .unblock/issues.jsonl confirmed zero durable-record hits for any of them. Approved design, all forks resolved by Miguel: (1) repo-level .knowledge/ — memories/ (atomic facts: frontmatter + curated index) + wiki/ (runs/ per-session run-reports, topics/ runbooks, index.md); (2) wiki is descriptive, NEVER normative — hierarchy stays PRD > spine > crate plans; nothing normative originates in .knowledge (guards the standing no-standalone-design-docs rule); (3) the run-report template carries a MANDATORY glossary defining every session-local id used (what it is + where it lives); (4) issue comments remain the per-task spine — short, self-contained per the clarity rule, linking to the wiki page for detail; (5) same-commit rule extends: work + issues.jsonl re-export + run-report in one commit/PR; (6) the clarity rule (expand session-local ids on first mention; durable ids get a one-clause anchor; fork questions name their object) lands in PROCESS.md §7 within this package; (7) enforcement is HARD from day 1 (Miguel's explicit resolution — block, never warn): a separate xtask doc-lint class + a CI PR gate + PreToolUse hooks; (8) the repo is PUBLIC — a Miguel-stamped privacy triage gates the private-memory migration (task .3) and the triage list itself never enters the repo; (9) the format stays migration-friendly to the roadmap §7 docs-in-DB knowledge layer — .knowledge is its file-based precursor; (10) CLAUDE.md gets one doc-map pointer row, never an @import of wiki content. comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
EPIC COMPLETE (2026-07-27). All children closed and merged: .1 spec (design gate closed after three iterations), .2 scaffold + .4 day-1 enforcement (PR #428), .6 post-merge activation (PR-gate made a REQUIRED check via a repository ruleset, plus the live hook-wiring canaries), .7 removal of the unused ACP tool coverage (PR #429, Miguel's call), .3 migration of the stamped 49-memory subset (PR #430), .5 the knowledge gardener (PR #431).

What now exists on main: .knowledge/ with 49 atomic memories, 4 run-reports and the first topic runbook, each behind a curated index; hard day-1 enforcement in three layers (the knowledge-lint structural checks, the run-report gate as a required CI check with the same predicate run by a pre-PR hook, and the PreToolUse guards protecting the memories tree and the sanctioned retire flow); the clarity rule in PROCESS section 7; and a supervised recurring gardener (a weekly reminder keeps one standing issue open; a session runs the documented sweep with a human in the loop).

Proof it works, not just ships: the enforcement blocked real attempts during this session (a nested memory write, a recursive delete into the tree, and a pull-request creation missing its run-report), and the inaugural gardener sweep found and fixed sixteen memories, including two factual errors that would have actively misled a future session. Both quality gates caught real defects rather than rubber-stamping — the enforcement gate found an over-broad exemption that would have left a hole, and the gardener gate found a durable lesson accidentally deleted along with the stale status around it.

ONE OPEN FOLLOW-UP, not blocking this epic and deliberately left to Miguel: the 49 migrated memories now exist in BOTH the assistant's private store and the public repo, which will drift over time. The choice is to make the repo the single home (removing the migrated copies privately, keeping only the held-private items plus a pointer) or to accept the duplication. Nothing decided; it is not tracked as a task yet because it concerns a private store outside this repo.

comments.text:
Verify quality gate, round 1 (2026-07-23; code-reviewer + qa-expert + rust-engineer + coordinator, branch knowledge-layer-landing): VERDICT = FAIL — returns to Implement (first of the two allowed iterations). The enforcement is otherwise real: every suite green, and all seven mandated adversarial probes came back red from the SHIPPED artifacts, not just the fixtures (an orphan page; an unknown frontmatter key; a glossary missing a code; a repo doc renamed into the knowledge tree; an export-only comment that coins a code; a nested import of the knowledge tree) — each correctly blocked, no hard-enforcement softening survived elsewhere, no bypass path found. Two blocking must-fixes.

First, a real hole in the hard-enforcement guarantee. The placeholder-file exemption the implementer added so the empty wiki topics directory can be committed is too broad: it skips any file named .gitkeep in all three content directories with no emptiness check. So an agent could write a .gitkeep holding arbitrary prose into the memories directory and it would ship completely unchecked — the whole knowledge tree is stripped from the PR gate, so the lint is the only guard and it waves this through. The reviewer proved a non-empty placeholder is accepted with a clean exit, and the implementer's on-record claim that the exemption was scoped to exactly the topics placeholder is false. The fix is NOT to remove the placeholder (the topics directory needs it so a fresh clone passes the structure guard) but to narrow the skip to exactly the topics directory AND require the file be zero bytes, falling through to the normal stray-file finding otherwise, with tests pinning rejection of a non-empty topics placeholder and of a placeholder in either other directory, plus a corrected code comment.

Second, the committed tracker record on the branch is stale. The exported issues file was frozen at the implement-start handoff, so it carries this task's start note but not the implement-outcome summary or the deviation ledger (which currently live only in the live tracker and as gotchas in the run-report). The same-commit rule this landing itself establishes requires that authoritative ledger to be in the committed record for you to ratify at PR review. The fix, in the same commit as the first: re-export the issues file so it carries the full current thread, and — because the glossary check scans the linked issues' comments up to the run-report date — reconcile the run-report glossary so every code in the newly-captured comments has a row, proven green by re-running the knowledge lint before committing.

The placeholder-file mechanism itself stays flagged for your ratification at PR review regardless of the fix. The other five flagged deviations were ruled sound; one still owes four live-session hook-wiring checks that can only run after merge (hooks load from the merged settings, and testing them before merge would mean mutating the shared working tree, which is forbidden) — I'll surface that as a PR-review item. Full code-anchored detail is in the Verify verdict file, which rides into the run-report. Looping back to Implement now in an isolated worktree; the re-verify targets these two fixes plus a no-regression sweep. If it also fails, I escalate to you rather than looping a third time.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand map (2026-09-11), off main at 34557b9. graph: used (codebase-memory index at 34557b9; it confirmed the single caller chain dispatch -> commands/mcp.rs::run -> run_mcp_server -> run_mcp_server_handler, and that server.rs:464 is the only production composition of the transport stack). Team: Plan, rust-engineer, research-analyst lenses in isolated worktrees, multi-agent-coordinator synthesis. No cargo was run by the team (a concurrent session shares the target dir); compile-level claims below are marked unverified.

MECHANISM, verified in rmcp 1.7.0 src/service/server.rs:172-204. A pre-handshake ping request is answered with an empty result (:178-189) and the loop continues. Any other request breaks the loop at :191 and fails the initialize match at :200-204, returning ExpectedInitializeRequest(Some(frame)) with NOTHING written to the client first. Any non-request frame (notification, response, error) takes the other arm at :192-196 and returns the same error. The error becomes McpServerError::Transport, then INTERNAL_ERROR, then exit 1. rmcp 1.8.0 leaves this loop untouched (its diff is version negotiation only), so no pinned-version bump closes the class.

THE CLASS IS ALREADY NORMATIVE in docs/PRD.md:131 (the D48 row, clause 6(i)) and repeated at docs/plans/00-roadmap.md:258-261: any first frame that is neither initialize nor ping, request or notification alike. The spine is silent on it (docs/plans/01-design-spine.md:3333 and :522 enumerate only Cancelled and ConnectionClosed as named mcp Err classes), and the spine has no section describing the transport's read-side behaviour at all; D43 and D47 live in PRD rows plus wire.rs prose. So the decision needs a spine home minted, not only a PRD row.

SEAMS. (1) crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:464, the only production composition: VersionClampingTransport::new(DupScanningTransport::new(read, write)); the unclamped test-util helper at :614-630 bypasses both wrappers by design. (2) crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs:333-364, the D47 answer-and-drop arm; a gate must sit BELOW it, because a D47 frame's id lives only in the raw bytes and a gate keyed on the parsed message would turn the recovered-id answer into an id-less one that releases no peer. (3) wire.rs:242-251, answer_error, the single byte-atomic emission helper. (4) wire.rs:261-276, send() takes &mut self and its head runs synchronously before the async block, so a plain bool latch flipped on the outbound InitializeResult is settable there; the clamp at server.rs:522-527 forwards send synchronously, so the latch reaches the inner transport. Alternative latch point: the inbound initialize request passed upward from receive(), one frame earlier and behaviourally identical, because rmcp reads no further line between the two points (:191 to :240).

WHAT EACH SHAPE WOULD GET. A premature request can be answered out-of-band on its own typed id (the D47 arm with a different ErrorData) and dropped. A premature notification, response or error frame gets no reply, because JSON-RPC 2.0 section 4.1 forbids replying to a notification and a response/error frame is itself a reply. The ub-nbz reply-loss race does not bite pre-handshake: expect_next_message awaits receive() bare (:134-137) with no competing select arm; the unbiased select exists only after the handshake (service.rs:805-813).

THREE COSTS, SIZED. (a) Harness: seven bare DupScanningTransport::new sites in wire.rs test modules (:774, :950, :1020, :1051, :1179, :1407, :1442) build a transport with no service attached, so a send-side latch never opens in the CD-7 parity harness (:757-804) and the mostly non-ping corpus (:537-697) collapses parity if the gate is hosted inside DupScanningTransport. A separate decorator between clamp and scan leaves :757-804 unchanged; a receive-side latch plus an initialize prefix frame in the corpus keeps one constructor and no test-only seam. (b) Inversions: crates/unblock-cli/tests/mcp_lifecycle.rs:417-463 (the D38 no-signal run-loop cell) provokes its Err with notifications/initialized at :422 and carries D48's only end-to-end stderr-payload witness for the run-loop-Err route (:448-462); :620-650 (the D47 control cell for an id-less notification) inverts from exit 1 to exit 0; both docstrings state the class as live prose. After the gate the only wire-reachable unsignalled run-loop Err is TransportError (a broken pipe on the pre-handshake ping reply is a genuine, injection-free provocation, but McpClient.stdout at tests/common/mod.rs:268 is private and Linux pipe semantics must be observed on CI). ExpectedInitializeRequest becomes wire-unreachable, so the D49 describe_frame render at crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs:104-136 turns into defence-in-depth; its unit pin over the test-util constructor was written for that day (docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:94). (c) Cascade: docs/PRD.md:131 clause 6(i) and :132; docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:91 and :94 (the owning crate plan, which repeats "delivering a notification in the initialize slot kills the server" as D47's drop justification); wire.rs:50-52 (same claim as module doc, must be restated, not deleted); 00-roadmap.md:257-261, :293, :328-329, :338; implementation-plan.md:196, :287; scripts/checks/d48-stdout-channel-claims.sh:131 (a presence grep whose description says OPEN, so it stays green and rots silently); d49-startup-failure-render-claims.sh:108, :148, :195; .github/workflows/ci.yml:345; docs/roadmap.html:416-417 (outside the doc-lint corpus). A new D-id triggers the D-range cascade at three prose sites and six required check scripts.

ECOSYSTEM EVIDENCE (research lens, from source). All four MCP spec revisions carry only the sender-side sentence (the client SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings before the initialize response) and state no receipt obligation. LSP 3.17 is explicitly asymmetric: a premature request gets -32002 ServerNotInitialized, notifications are dropped, the server survives. The TypeScript SDK has no pre-initialize gate at all (serves the frame; unknown method -32601; notifications dropped). The C# SDK answers a JSON-RPC error and stays alive. The Python SDK v1.9 dies on a premature request by accident and survives a premature notification; its main branch deleted the guard entirely. Upstream rmcp main now writes -32602 before STILL dying on the request arm (rust-sdk issue #1157 is this defect's sibling) and stays byte-silent on the non-request arm; rust-sdk issue #783 / PR #788 accepted the argument that the spec constrains what each side sends, not what it rejects. Killing the server is done only by rmcp and by Python's request arm. No host was found sending a non-ping FIRST frame (VS Code's early logging/setLevel sits after the initialize response), so that part stays unproven.

OPTIONS carried into Decide, each with evidence above: gate all four shapes and answer a premature request -32600 while dropping the other three; gate requests only; buffer and replay after the handshake (matches rmcp's own comment at server.rs:250-255 that a pre-initialized request is processed normally, but costs an unbounded pre-handshake queue while the D31 write lock is held; replaying a response/error is provably a no-op because Peer has sent nothing); host the gate in a new decorator between clamp and scan, inside DupScanningTransport below the D47 arm, or inside the clamp (whose name, CD-6 pin and deletion endgame at server.rs:488-503 would stop describing it); upgrade rmcp instead (closes only the silence half, keeps the death).

UNVERIFIED, for the orchestrator to measure: the exit codes and stdout bytes of the four first-frame shapes on the built binary; whether a plain bool latch satisfies the Send + 'static bound on send()'s future and does not collide with the line_buf borrow at wire.rs:293-297; whether the parity tier really goes red under a scanner-hosted gate; whether the broken-pipe provocation returns BrokenPipe on Linux CI.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Decide (2026-09-11). Team: Plan, rust-engineer, research-analyst lenses in isolated worktrees plus multi-agent-coordinator reconciliation; all three lenses converged on every fork and the coordinator re-verified the decisive claims in rmcp source. Miguel resolved the forks as recorded below. This change mints its own decision id, D50, per the issue text and the D48 row (docs/PRD.md:131 clause 6(i)).

ORCHESTRATOR MEASUREMENTS on the built binary (1.0.1-rc.3 tag, handshake path unchanged since) in a throwaway workspace, one spawn per case. ping, then initialize, then initialized: exit 0, normal handshake. tools/list as the first frame: exit 1, stdout 0 bytes, the structured INTERNAL_ERROR document on stderr, and the child exits even with stdin kept open, so a stdio client observes EOF rather than waiting forever (this corrects a lens claim that the client stays pending). notifications/cancelled first, a response frame first, an error frame first, notifications/initialized first: each exit 1, stdout 0 bytes, INTERNAL_ERROR on stderr. tools/list sent after the initialize response but before notifications/initialized: served normally, exit 0, so rmcp does not gate on the initialized notification and the new gate must not either.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE TEXT. The claim that a live-but-unhandshaken server "has taken the D31 write lock" is false. Session::acquire (crates/unblock-engine/src/session/write.rs:122-126) takes the in-process permit and then the file lock once per mutation, and the MutationGuard (crates/unblock-engine/src/permit.rs) releases both at the end of that mutation; storage opens a fresh descriptor per acquire and unlocks on guard drop (crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/lock.rs:60-66, :212). The one pre-handshake acquisition is migrate() (crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/mod.rs:605-618), released when workspace open returns. A server parked before initialize holds an open libsql connection, its pipes and an in-process semaphore, and blocks no other writer. The gate's justification is availability and client-visible behaviour, never contention relief, and no D50 prose may repeat the lock framing.

RESOLUTIONS.
1. Scope: the gate intercepts all four JSON-RPC frame shapes (request, notification, response, error); only initialize and ping pass through before the handshake. Reason: the class is already product truth at docs/PRD.md:131 clause 6(i) and :132 already prices the interception as removing both live paths; rmcp collapses the three non-request shapes into one arm (rmcp-1.7.0/src/service/server.rs:192-196), and the id-less notification is the cheapest kill an untrusted peer has under NFR-18. Requests-only would narrow a shipped row.
2. Disposition: a premature request is answered -32600 Invalid Request on its own id and dropped; a premature notification, response or error frame is dropped with no reply, because JSON-RPC 2.0 section 4.1 forbids replying to a notification and a reply to a reply is meaningless. Reason: rmcp writes nothing on either death route today (Peer::new only runs at server.rs:205), so the client's only current signal is the child's death; a surviving server that drops silently would turn today's fast failure into an unbounded hang for an rmcp client, which awaits untimed (crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs:47-48). -32600 reuses the byte path D47 ships at wire.rs:242-251. -32002 collides with this server's resource-not-found mapping (crates/unblock-mcp/src/error.rs:14-17); -32602 misdescribes the fault. Buffer-and-replay was rejected: it retains an unbounded accumulator on the least-identified path, a byte bound needs an overflow policy that re-asks the same fork, and replaying notifications is dead work because UnblockServer overrides no notification handler (rmcp defaults are ready(()) at rmcp-1.7.0/src/handler/server.rs:296-321).
3. Home and latch: a NEW transport decorator, its own type, module and cells, slotted between VersionClampingTransport and DupScanningTransport at crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:464, so the receive order is scan, gate, clamp and the gate sees a frame AFTER the D47 answer-and-drop arm (wire.rs:333-364), which is required because a D47 frame's id lives only in the raw bytes. The gate OPENS when the server's own initialize response, a ServerJsonRpcMessage::Response carrying ServerResult::InitializeResult, passes through the decorator's send(), the edge the spec names ("before the server has responded to the initialize request"); the pre-handshake ping reply (ServerResult::EmptyResult) must not open it, and the latch keys on the variant, never on anything the clamp can rewrite. Reason for the decorator: hosting the gate inside DupScanningTransport would close the latch for every entry of the CD-7 differential corpus, since run_ours (wire.rs:943-955) feeds each entry as a standalone stream, so the per-entry tier (wire.rs:1221-1255) and the whole-stream tier (:757-804) would diverge from rmcp on nearly the whole corpus; the decorator leaves that harness byte-unchanged and still writes through the scanner's send under the same mutex (wire.rs:261-276). The clamp is disqualified by its stated deletion endgame (server.rs:488-503). Reason for the send-side latch over the team's receive-side recommendation: the two edges are separated by zero inbound frames in rmcp 1.7.0 (no receive between the break at server.rs:191 and the write at :240-248), so they behave identically today, and the send-side edge is the one the spec names and stays correct if a future rmcp reads ahead; the receive-side edge was only preferred for a bare-transport host, which the decorator choice removes. The decorator's reply is written inside receive() and inherits the ub-nbz cancellable-write residual; pre-handshake the only dropper is the cancellation select (server.rs:150-155), the regime measured at 0 of 40 losses, and the module doc must say so.
4. Witness: the shipped D38 cell (crates/unblock-cli/tests/mcp_lifecycle.rs:417-463) is repointed at a broken pipe on the pre-handshake ping reply: the test closes its own read end of the child's stdout (a new McpClient method beside close_stdin at tests/common/mod.rs:538; write_without_reading at :517 keeps the pipe open and is unusable), sends a pre-handshake ping, and rmcp's own reply write (server.rs:178-189, context "sending pre-init ping response") fails with BrokenPipe into ServerInitializeError::TransportError, the ONE unsignalled run-loop Err still wire-reachable after the gate (ExpectedInitializeRequest becomes unreachable; ExpectedInitializedNotification is never constructed; UnexpectedInitializeResponse and InitializeFailed are unreachable because UnblockServer declares no initialize override; UnsupportedProtocolVersion is unreachable because the version newtype's partial_cmp is total; ConnectionClosed is D40-delegated to exit 0; Cancelled is the signal path). The gate's OWN failed reply write cannot carry the witness: it returns None from receive() and lands on D40's exit 0 (crates/unblock-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:202-205). The cell keeps the exit-1 and stderr-payload halves and loses its stdout-frame-free half by construction; the old assertions stay until the new cell is green on Linux CI, because a macOS probe has masked a Linux pipe path in this repo before. If Linux proves flaky, the fallback is the unit pin alone (commands/mcp.rs:628), never leaving a frame shape fatal to preserve a test. The D47 control cell (:620-650) inverts from exit 1 to exit 0 and both docstrings are rewritten in the same commit.

CASCADE owed by the Spec phase: PRD D50 row plus reciprocal notes on D47, D48 clause 6(i) and D49 (its render becomes defence-in-depth; docs/PRD.md:132 still describes a live startup failure); spine section 5b and, following D47's spine footprint, the transport read side gains its first normative sentences; docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:90-94 (line 90 already describes the stdio bind with no decorators); wire.rs:50-52 and unblock-mcp.md:91 restate D47's drop justification instead of resting it on the fixed fatality; 00-roadmap.md:257-261, :293, :328-329, :338; implementation-plan.md:196, :287; the D-range bump at CLAUDE.md, ci-cd section 2.1(a), xtask/src/doc_lint.rs and the RANGE_RE knobs of the six required check scripts; a new scripts/checks/d50-*.sh wired as a required doc-lint step; the ub-kp7 rows in d48-stdout-channel-claims.sh:131 and d49-startup-failure-render-claims.sh:108, :148; .github/workflows/ci.yml:345; docs/roadmap.html:416-417. D47's precedent decides whether the contract version moves (it answered -32600 out-of-band and unblock.mcp.v1.9 stood). Exit-code stance to reconcile explicitly with D35 and the D48 acceptance text: a premature frame followed by EOF now exits 0 through D40 because the failure no longer exists, the same additive bug-fix reading D40 itself shipped under after GA.

MUST-FIXES (each blocks the gate).
1. docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:93 and implementation-plan.md T3.13 scope: the spec never says how the gate recognises initialize and ping. rmcp's ClientRequest is an untagged union whose last arm is CustomRequest (rmcp-1.7.0/src/model.rs:3241, :3269-3289), so a frame spelled method "initialize" with untypeable params decodes as CustomRequest while rmcp keys on the variant at both edges (server.rs:176, :200-204). A method-string key would pass that frame up and rmcp would still die, falsifying the three new "unreachable from the wire" sentences. title: Bug: a first frame that is neither `initialize` nor `ping` kills the MCP server, even with a healthy workspace open

description:
Found 2026-08-07 by the ub-gwe Verify gate, by MUTATION rather than by reading — which matters, because this exact class of coverage claim has been cleared twice before by read-only review and was wrong both times.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. In a private checkout, the entire hard-rules bullet that ub-gwe rewrites (the one making the code graph the first move for structural questions, at CLAUDE.md line 37) was DELETED. All six scripts under scripts/checks/ stayed at exit 0 and the doc-lint reported OK across its nineteen-file corpus. Merely breaking the contiguity of the phrase "discovery, not authority" inside it was equally invisible. The probe was proven non-vacuous by a positive control: the same undefined-decision-id and non-canonical-command bytes injected into a file that IS in the doc-lint corpus produced two findings, so the tooling works and simply does not look at this file.

WHY THAT IS A GAP RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE. CLAUDE.md is not in the doc-lint corpus, which is correct — that corpus is the nineteen normative documents under docs/. But CLAUDE.md is the always-in-context operational contract, and the repo has already decided, repeatedly, that a claim worth relying on gets an executable anchor rather than a convention: that is the whole reason the scripts/checks/ family exists, and the reason the process guide's own list of files carrying the live decision range is pinned by a script instead of by a derived count.

THE CONCRETE EXPOSURE. An acceptance criterion at docs/plans/implementation-plan.md line 77 restates this rule, citing it by the phrase "discovery, not authority". That file IS in the doc-lint corpus. So the repo has a corpus-protected criterion whose subject lives in an unprotected file — the criterion survives a deletion of the very rule it grades. The coupling between them is prose alone.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, as the gate proposed it. A row in the scripts/checks/ family asserting the rule's presence in CLAUDE.md, in the style of the existing rows that pin script names into docs/PROCESS.md so that a count-free list cannot rot silently. Whether that belongs in a new script or as rows on an existing one is part of the design, and so is which of the five hard rules deserve anchoring — this issue is not an argument for pinning every sentence of an always-in-context file, which would make ordinary editing hostile.

RELATED, and worth reading together: issue ub-tge, the sibling finding that the file-level presence check on CLAUDE.md enforces only PRESENCE and not the "exactly one occurrence" its rationale claims. Both are about the same unprotected file and may share one fix.

### Acceptance Criteria
- A decision is recorded on WHICH hard rules earn an executable anchor and which deliberately do not, with the reasoning. Anchoring all five by default is a decision, not a given.
- Whatever is anchored is proven by mutation, not asserted: deleting or corrupting the anchored text makes a required job exit non-zero on exactly that row, and a positive control shows the probe is not vacuous.
- The anchor is wired into the same required job as its siblings, so its red is actually observed.
- The prose-only coupling between docs/plans/implementation-plan.md line 77 and the CLAUDE.md rule it grades is either made executable or explicitly recorded as convention-only, so the next reader does not have to rediscover it by mutation.
- The anchor's own maintenance cost is stated: what a future editor of that CLAUDE.md line must also update, and where that instruction lives.

## Diagnosis ESTABLISHED (2026-07-21) — root cause is NOT what this issue assumed, and scope widens 4-lens adversarial investigation (workflow wf_cffc3ecd-7fc, 9 agents, 4 independent live reproductions on the 1.0.1-rc.1 binary). The M6 "root cause undiagnosed" constraint can now be LIFTED for the server-side mechanism. ### What actually happens `body` IS genuinely required on the Add arm (crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/comment.rs:51-58; spine 01-design-spine.md:1898; published `"required":["action","issue_id","body"]` in tests/snapshots/contract_suite__schema_bundle.snap:4157-4161). A payload carrying `content` is rejected by plain serde INSIDE rmcp's `Parameters

` extractor (rmcp-1.7.0/src/handler/server/tool.rs:185-195 -> `ErrorData::invalid_params`), short-circuiting BEFORE the tool body. server.rs:152 returns that `Err(ErrorData)` verbatim; the only in-band re-band in the handler is the adjacent :154 rate-limit arm. Wire result: `{"id":3,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"failed to deserialize parameters: missing field `body`"}}` — no `result`, no `structuredContent`, no `isError`. So "persisted nothing" is correct-by-construction, NOT a storage defect. `preflight`, `Session::add_comment` and `ok_json`/`err_json` never execute. The observed "OK + empty structuredContent" is a CLIENT-side rendering of a `result`-less protocol error (inferred — no harness is checked into this repo, so do not assert "returns OK" as server behaviour in any doc). ### The defect is therefore an error-CHANNEL defect, and it has TWO arms - **(a)** a missing REQUIRED field escapes out-of-band as JSON-RPC -32602, never reaching the contracted in-band structured-error channel (FR-11 `code`/`message`/`hint`/`retryable`). - **(b)** an unknown / misspelled OPTIONAL field is silently DISCARDED and returns `isError:false`. Live-proven: `issue create {"prioriti":0,"descriptionn":"LOST BODY TEXT"}` returned success, created an issue with default priority and NO description; `sync export {"pathh":...}` wrote the DEFAULT path. **Arm (b) is the genuine silent data loss** and is the one phenomenologically matching the original report. Routing (a) in-band does nothing for (b). ### Scope: surface-wide, all 8 tools — not comment-specific All 8 take `Parameters` then `self.preflight(&input)` (comment.rs:90-96, issue.rs:262-265, claim.rs:46-47, defer.rs:48-49, dep.rs:93-94, query.rs:77-78, sync.rs:59-60, diagnostics.rs:84-86). `preflight` re-serializes the ALREADY-deserialized typed value (server.rs:101-109), so it structurally cannot see a field serde dropped. `grep -rn 'invalid_params|32602' crates/` = **0 hits** — the class is entirely unhandled and entirely untested. ### Contributory crates/unblock-model/src/validation.rs:104,109,136-137 labels the empty-body error field `"content"` (declared deliberate "bd wire parity") — unblock's own error vocabulary names the exact wrong field the agent typed. Renaming it is itself a contract change; leaving it means the fixed error still misdirects. UNRESOLVED. ### Doc root of the blind spot 01-design-spine.md:2159 asserts "Oversized/invalid args are rejected by schemars validation before reaching the engine (NFR-18)". schemars 1.2.1 is codegen-only; there is no runtime validator. The sentence is FALSE and must be corrected spec-first (PROCESS §2) before any code. Note this puts the SPINE (high tier) on this issue's side; `invalid_params` is pinned only at docs/plans/crates/unblock-mcp.md:26, the lowest tier, and descriptively. ### MIGUEL'S DECISION (2026-07-21) **v1.0.1 fixes BOTH arms** — not arm (a) alone. Accepted consequence: rejecting unknown fields emits `additionalProperties:false` into all 8 advertised inputSchemas, moving CONTRACT_HASH and forcing CONTRACT_VERSION v1.5 -> v1.6 inside a patch release, and turning previously-accepted calls into rejections. This strains roadmap:88 "maintenance only — no FR is added or re-tiered"; that line needs revisiting in the same cascade. The NFR-18 quota bypass found alongside is filed as its own P0 in the same slot — and it CONSTRAINS the fix shape: only raw-payload (`JsonObject`) hand-deserialization lets `enforce_quota` see unknown keys, which is the same seam that gives arm (b)'s rejection. The three fixes converge on one L7 boundary change. ### Open risk to re-verify BEFORE committing implementation scope serde documents `deny_unknown_fields` as incompatible with `#[serde(flatten)]`, and there are **22 flatten sites** in crates/unblock-mcp. One lens claims it compiles anyway against serde =1.0.228; another disputes it. If the restriction holds, arm (b) requires per-tool `JsonObject` hand-deserialization across those sites — a materially different cost. Settle this empirically first. ### Also required CONTRACT_HASH blind spot: options.rs:39-53 scopes the hash to `(capabilities(), schema_bundle())` only, so error-channel ROUTING is invisible to the FR-12 gate — it neither blocks nor protects a regression here. Any fix must ship with a live-wire pinned test. There is currently ZERO coverage of this class.

## Spec/Plan complete + Miguel's rulings (2026-07-21) — workflow wf_eed82e64-80c

Plan file: scratchpad/v101-mcp-boundary-plan.md (9 sections). Design Review gate running as wf_900a4bbb-44f.

### MIGUEL RULED (both blocking forks closed)
1. **The input tightening ships in v1.0.1 as a DEFECT FIX, not a 2.0.0 break.** Decisive evidence: docs/PRD.md:175 — the FR-20 `[must]` acceptance criterion — already promises "tool input is schema-validated (`schemars`) and rejects oversized/invalid args". Today's code therefore FAILS a shipped must-AC; fixing it is not a behaviour change to any working call, since the only inputs newly rejected are ones currently destroyed in silence.
2. **Contract-surface scope for v1.0.1 = the CONTRACT_HASH gate widening (B2) ONLY.** outputSchema and serde aliases defer to v1.1 as two new issues.

### Feasibility SETTLED — the expensive branch is dead
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` DOES work with `#[serde(flatten)]` on the workspace serde 1.0.228. Independently re-verified by the orchestrator against a pinned scratch crate replicating the real flatten shape:
```
GOOD -> Ok("ok")
TYPO -> Err(Error("unknown field `descriptionn`", line: 1, column: 32))
```
serde_derive emits a post-flatten leftover scan; the documented "incompatible with flatten" restriction is stale. Cost collapses from 22 hand-written deserializers to ~10 one-line attributes on OUTER containers.

**Three placement rules are load-bearing:**
- `deny` on a flatten TARGET is a silent no-op — outer containers only.
- `deny` is NOT recursive — each nested non-flattened struct needs its own (DepInput confirmed).
- `deny` ALONE converts facet (b) into facet (a): all rejections would arrive as out-of-band -32602. **(a) and (b) MUST co-land.** Never split them.

### Recommended design (plan §3, pending the Review gate)
New `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/args.rs`: a crate-local `Parameters<T>` — deliberately shadowing rmcp's by name — whose `FromContextPart` stores raw `context.arguments` WITHOUT deserializing, making rmcp's -32602 arm (tool.rs:185-195) structurally unreachable, and whose `JsonSchema` delegates to T (hash-neutral on its own).

Ordered prologue on the RAW value, in one shared method:
1. `enforce_quota` on the raw payload — closes (c); DELETE `preflight` (server.rs:101-109 measures the re-serialized TYPED value — that IS the bug).
2. Strip `_`-prefixed reserved keys AFTER measurement, so `_meta` is neither a bypass channel nor falsely rejected.
3. `from_value::<T>` under serde_path_to_error with deny_unknown_fields — closes (b).
4. Map failures to `StructuredError{VALIDATION_FAILED, hint, context{field,kind}}` via the existing `err_json` — closes (a).

**FLAGGED TO THE REVIEW GATE, not accepted:** the name-shadowing is load-bearing (rmcp-macros `find_parameters_type_in_sig` matches the last path-segment ident `Parameters`; any other name silently degrades all 8 inputSchemas to empty). A maintainer "fixing" the import back to rmcp's silently reinstates the bug. Documented fallback is `#[tool(input_schema=...)]`. The gate rules on this, not the orchestrator.

### Scope changes to this issue
- **ub-lp9.19 (quota) FOLDS INTO THIS PR** — (c)'s fix IS the prologue ordering in the new seam and cannot be implemented independently. Issue stays open for tracking; closes on the same merge.
- **B2 gate widening folds in too**, no new issue: CONTRACT_HASH widened to the ordered triple (capabilities(), schema_bundle(), aggregate_tool_router().list_all()), plus an assertion that `list_all()[i].input_schema == schema_for_type::<T>()` so the extractor can never silently go dark, plus a transport-level channel matrix (a hash cannot express a channel).
- Contract consequence: schemars emits `additionalProperties:false` per oneOf arm -> schema_bundle() bytes move -> **CONTRACT_VERSION v1.5 -> v1.6 + CONTRACT_HASH re-pin**. Additive within 1.x per D35.
- ONE PR for cascade + (a)+(b)+(c) + B2: they share the single v1.6 bump and one golden re-bless. Splitting burns v1.7 and splits the re-bless in two — precisely when a bad golden slips through.

### HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED — do not carry it forward
The theory that a degraded `tools/list` schema was the proximate cause is **wrong**. Over real JSON-RPC, `tools/list[i].inputSchema` is byte-identical to `schema_bundle()[tool].input` for all 8 tools — full oneOf, 66 required entries, `comment.add` correctly declaring `required:["action","issue_id","body"]`. The "Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of..." prose has ZERO hits in the repo and ZERO in rmcp-1.7.0/src: the MCP *client's* renderer synthesizes it. No doc or commit message may assert that causal chain. Per M6, nothing asserts "returns OK" as server behaviour either.

### Tests (plan §5)
New `crates/unblock-cli/tests/error_channel.rs` (must live in cli — mcp_round_trip.rs precedent), needing a new `McpClient::call_tool_envelope` because today's `call_tool` asserts the error member away and structurally cannot express this class. Matrix: 8 tools x 3 malformations asserting `resp.error is None` (the channel invariant no hash can express), isError true, VALIDATION_FAILED, retryable false, non-empty hint, context.field. Plus the (c) unknown-key regression WITH its known-key control as a pair, nested-deny coverage, `_meta` acceptance, and happy-path non-vacuity via a flattened `agent_name`.

**Highest-risk failure mode:** a missed nested `deny` attribute leaves facet (b) live SILENTLY with a green suite. The per-container mutation expectations are the only guard.

## CORRECTION to comment #8, + Review gate verdict + Miguel's 3 rulings (2026-07-21)

### CORRECTION — retract "Storage is NOT implicated"
Comment #8 (and the earlier diagnosis comment) stated flatly that **storage is not implicated**. That is FALSE AS A GENERAL CLAIM and must not be carried forward. It is true only for the comment-add write path, which is what was actually probed.

Verified directly in the tree (2026-07-21): `crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/deps.rs:86-96` binds **5 of 6** columns —
```
INSERT INTO dependencies (issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by)
```
`DepInput.metadata` is **accepted, typed, and published in the schema, then silently discarded at L2**. That is facet (b)'s exact harm — a silent drop behind `isError:false` — one layer BELOW where the L7 seam can reach. Reachable both via the `dep` tool and via `CreateInput.deps`.

Second survivor, same class: `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/bulk_markdown.rs:202` — `Section::Unknown => {} // ignore unknown sections.` — with a test asserting the drop as correct behaviour. Consequence if unaddressed: after the fix the SAME tool would reject `descriptionn` on `create` and swallow `### Descriptoin` on `create_bulk`, and the rewritten FR-20 AC would be false the day it was written.

### Design Review gate: PASS_WITH_MUST_FIXES (wf_900a4bbb-44f, 4 adversarial lenses + coordinator)
All four lenses returned pass_with_must_fixes. The design CORE survived independent re-verification on every axis and is **adopted, not revisitable**: the deferring `Parameters<T>` seam (the rmcp macro really does match on the last path-segment ident — verified in both 1.7 and 1.8), `deny_unknown_fields` coexisting with flatten and internally-tagged enums, the three placement rules, the byte-identical JsonSchema delegation, and the v1.5->v1.6 bump.

What the gate rejected was the plan's periphery. 11 must-fixes, 16 should-fixes, full text appended as "## REVIEW GATE (2026-07-21)" in the plan file. The four that change the shape:
- **MF#2 — DELETE the `_`-prefix strip.** Premise was false: `_meta`/`task` are SIBLINGS of `arguments` on `CallToolRequestParams` (rmcp model.rs:2956-2967) and are destructured away at tool.rs:44-49, so a conformant `_meta` never reaches `context.arguments`. The blanket strip protected nothing while making `{"action":"show","id":"x","_junk":"LOST"}` silently accepted — reopening facet (b) on a new path, permanently.
- **MF#3 — the proposed FR-12 AC was demonstrably FALSE.** `params.arguments=42` fails during `CallToolRequestParams` deserialization BEFORE `ToolCallContext::new`, so no args.rs seam reaches it; unknown tool names likewise stay out-of-band by design. Must be scoped, not absolute.
- **MF#5 — §3.5/§5.4 were UNCOMPILABLE.** `server.rs:82` declares `fn aggregate_tool_router()` — private (verified) — and the input types are `pub(crate)` while `contract_suite.rs` is an external crate. Pin against `schema_bundle()` instead (pub at schema.rs:73); stronger pin, no type exposure.
- **MF#1 — the highest-risk vacuity hole.** Replace "sweep for others" with a MECHANICAL guard: assert every object subschema in each of the 8 published inputSchemas carries `additionalProperties:false`, recursing oneOf/$defs/items. Note `CreateInput` needs its OWN attribute — the enum-level one does not reach the newtype variant `Create(Box<CreateInput>)`, so omitting it leaves the highest-traffic action silently lossy WHILE LOOKING COVERED.

The cascade also under-enumerated: 4 more Class-1 sites including a second PRD-level one (PRD:235, the NFR-18 threat model — the exact NFR facet (c) violates), plus an entire unenumerated doc class created by the folded-in B2 widening (~20 sites incl. code doc-comments), and two hard-RED `assert_eq!` pins missing from the v1.6 re-pin list.

### MIGUEL RULED (2026-07-21) — all three at the widest scope
1. **Both L2/out-of-seam facet-(b) survivors ENTER D42.** `create_bulk`'s ignored sections AND `dep.metadata`. Accepted cost: the dep.metadata fix is an **L2 storage change**, breaking the plan's "nothing below L7 touched" and widening the Verify surface during a data-integrity patch; the `bulk_markdown` test that asserts the drop must be INVERTED. Benefit: the rewritten FR-20 AC becomes true rather than true-by-omission.
2. **NFR-18 "per-request bytes" = the whole JSON-RPC `params`, and it closes NOW.** `params._meta`/`params.task` are unmeasured today — a 300000-byte blob was reproduced passing the 256 KiB cap (options.rs:79). `server.rs:144-156` already holds the whole params object, so the size check moves up. Without this the plan could not honestly claim to close a bypass channel.
3. **The B2 public-surface addition is accepted** — a `#[doc(hidden)] pub` accessor for the router descriptors, cascading to `tests/public_api.rs` and the spine §5 interface table.

### Consequence to face honestly
Scope now spans L2 + L7, inverts an existing asserted-behaviour test, and adds public surface. The roadmap:88 "maintenance only" rewrite must say this plainly rather than paper over it — that line is no longer merely strained, it is false as written.

NEXT: plan revision folding the 11 must-fixes + 16 should-fixes + these 3 rulings, then Implement. Implementation must NOT start from the current plan text.

## r2 REJECTED by the consistency pass + R3 RETRACTED (2026-07-21, wf_bfeed9a6-ed0)

The adversarial check on the revised plan returned `consistent: false`. The prediction that r2 would still carry a falsifiable claim held — it carried eleven.

### R3 IS RETRACTED — Miguel decided it on a false premise I supplied
I told Miguel that without a `#[doc(hidden)] pub` router-descriptor accessor, "the fix ships with its own new surface unpinned". **That is false.** Verified in the tree:
- `crates/unblock-mcp/tests/contract_suite.rs:116 live_list_tools_equals_the_builder_eight` already drives a real duplex and asserts the live `(name, description)` pairs are byte-identical to `capabilities().tools` for all 8 tools. Its own doc-comment at :104-114 states the rationale verbatim: *"every tool description is contract bytes TWICE ... mutating a live attribute literal left this whole suite — `contract_hash_matches_the_pinned_gate` included — GREEN, because the hash digests the CONSTANT, not the wire."*
- `contract_suite.rs:256 live_tools_input_schema_root_is_object` additionally pins every live `inputSchema` root.

The genuine residual gap is ONLY the live `input_schema` BODY, and r2's own anti-degradation pin against `schema_bundle()` — already `pub` at resources/schema.rs:73 — closes it with NO public-surface change. For every field unblock actually sets (name, description, input_schema), the third digest document is a pure function of documents 1+2; the only independently-hashable bytes left are `annotations`/`title`/`icons`, which unblock never sets.

**MIGUEL RULED: retract R3.** Drop the three-document digest widening AND the accessor. Keep only the anti-degradation pin. This also removes a name collision the check found: `fn tool_descriptors()` already exists at `crates/unblock-mcp/src/resources/capabilities.rs:81` building the OTHER descriptor surface — in a change whose stated premise is refusing "a second, divergent description of the input surface".

Process note worth recording: this repo's memory already carried the fact (*"an MCP tool description is contract bytes TWICE; pin with a (name,description) assert, GA-frozen"*) and it was not applied. Having the fact is not the same as checking it.

### Chronic defect in this lineage: the sweep tokens are wrong every generation
Three consecutive generations shipped a bad done-gate token — r1's width-bounded regex, the gate's "~28 hits", r2's repetition of it. Actual counts on main, verified:
```
git grep -nw schemars          -> 103   (plan says "~28, eyeballable")
git grep -n 'unblock\.mcp\.v1\.5' -> 19    (plan's re-pin table has 9)
git grep -nw CONTRACT_HASH     -> 109
two-document / both-discovery  -> 35    (plan says "~20")
```
The "frozen" container list says 11 in three places and 10 in a fourth; the real count is 10 (8 outer + CreateInput + DepInput), and §5.8 asks for 9 mutation rows for 8 outer containers. **r3 must DERIVE every count mechanically and record the command, not restate one.** A spec-first cascade whose done-gate is a count cannot ship with two of three counts wrong.

### Other blocking findings (full list in the r2 check output)
- §3.6 claims `Section::Unknown` appears at only two sites; it also appears at bulk_markdown.rs:90.
- §3.6's "re-introducing the drop becomes a compile error" is overstated: deleting the variant forces a new `None` arm at bulk_markdown.rs:141 which is itself a swallow site, unreachable only by virtue of the pre-scan. As drafted the drop RELOCATES rather than becoming impossible.
- §5.6 T10's margin analysis holds by ≤3 bytes and is unanalysed — three GA quota tests set `max_string_len: 16` and the new key-length check runs against `_meta`/`progressToken` (13). State the margin or a future fixture edit silently flips them.
- Several cited line numbers are off by 1-2 (quotas.rs:34,76,238 -> :35,75,236; §5.7 points at the assertion, not the digest fn at :29-40).

### MIGUEL RULED (2026-07-21) — two further scope calls
1. **The two ADDITIONAL create_bulk silent drops ENTER scope too** (beyond R1-i): (i) an invalid `### Priority` silently falls back to default (`tools/issue.rs:430-433` — `Priority::from_str` is fallible per unblock-model/src/enums/priority.rs:59-77), and (ii) a KNOWN H3 before the first `## ` is silently dropped (bulk_markdown.rs:134-143 runs the H3 branch only `if let Some(issue) = current_issue.as_mut()`). Both are isError:false on the same tool. Without them the rewritten FR-20 AC is false by omission again — exactly what R1 existed to prevent.
2. **`issue create` with deps is NON-ATOMIC — its own issue, OUT of this PR.** `create_issue` (storage/trait_def.rs:99) takes only the Issue, so deps land in a separate call: the issue can be created while its deps fail. This is a PRE-EXISTING GA data-integrity defect, not introduced here. It gets its own diagnosis rather than being fixed in passing inside a PR already spanning L2+L7.

NEXT: r3, deriving all counts mechanically. Implementation must not start from r2.

### What failed: the clerical layer, for the FOURTH consecutive generation

## Done-gate resolved: runtime assertions carry the weight, the script is demoted to lexical (2026-07-21, wf_3fb5d1f2-8b5 + wf_90f67b29-1b9)

### The executable done-gate was built, broken, hardened, and broken again
R7 replaced the prose counts with an executable script. A falsification pass then PROVED it passes vacuously — exit 0, "DONE-GATE PASSED (6 checks)", on a tree with zero behavioural change. Five bypass vectors were fixed, each with a watched fail-then-pass reproduction. A second adversarial pass broke it again with two NEW vectors that are the important ones:

**V2c — attribute FORM is not attribute SEMANTICS.**
```rust
#[serde(expecting = "an object" /* deny_unknown_fields */)]
```
rustc's lexer discards the block comment inside the attribute; the gate's regex does not. Thirteen containers spelled that way and CHECK 3 prints *"all 13 non-exempt input containers deny unknown fields"* — while a test executed on the same tree deserializes `{"kind":"ready","TOTALLY_UNKNOWN_ARG":42}` successfully.

**V2d — closing the DOCUMENT without closing the RUNTIME.** A 25-line `closed()` post-processor stamping `additionalProperties: false` onto every object node of each published inputSchema turns all 45 subschema violations green, keeps all 17 contract_suite tests passing, and changes nothing about what serde accepts. The cargo freshness proof — which resisted every laundering attempt and is genuinely sound — only proves snapshot == live DOCUMENT, and the document is produced by `schema_bundle()`, which the implementer writes. In review this is indistinguishable from the real fix; the repo already uses `#[schemars(extend("type" = "object"))]` for exactly that class of document-level stamp.

### The structural conclusion
**SIX of six checks assert over implementer-authored text** — not four, as the rescoped header claimed. Five patches to five spellings did not change the category: every new bypass was a different move against the same weakness. A doc-cascade gate is weak BY CATEGORY because the thing being checked and the thing doing the checking come from the same hand.

The falsification pass supplied the exit, and it was in the plan all along:
> a source-text check cannot decide this. Ask the compiler — a per-container assertion that `serde_json::from_str::<T>` REJECTS an unknown key. That is the §5.8 mutation table, and it is the only honest form of check 3.

A test that deserializes cannot be satisfied by annotation. No spelling, comment, or post-processor defeats it, because it does not read what was written — it executes what was compiled.

### MIGUEL RULED (2026-07-21) — R8
**The behavioural done-condition is runtime assertions; the script is demoted to lexical doc-cascade only.**
- Per input container: an assertion that `from_str::<T>` REJECTS a payload with an unknown key, and ACCEPTS the equivalent well-formed payload (the accept half is the non-vacuity guard). Already specified in §5.8 — it now carries the weight rather than supplementing a text check.
- The script keeps only the genuinely lexical checks over the doc cascade and the mechanical contract re-pin, with the four still-overstated SCOPE sentences corrected to lexical claims: it asserts that no live line matching a case-sensitive `schemars` token and one of five framing words survives — a result about five spellings, not about the document being true.
- No third hardening round. V2d is indistinguishable from legitimate work in review, so no static check can catch it; a sixth patch would be a sixth spelling.

### Proportion, recorded honestly
The behavioural change is ~10 serde attributes, one seam file, one missing storage bind, three markdown rejections, and their tests. The verification apparatus around it consumed more workflow rounds than the change will consume lines. That was defensible for a data-integrity patch on a GA product — and the apparatus did earn its keep: it falsified four confident orchestrator claims, caught a false `[must]` AC twice, an uncompilable pin, a strip built on a false premise, and a gate that greened an untouched tree. But the part worth keeping was specified by r3, and everything after it was the apparatus auditing itself.

NEXT: Implement, as an isolated-worktree team per PROCESS §4.

UNDERSTAND phase complete (2026-08-03) — three read-only specialists plus a coordinator, no repo file touched. Full map: `.knowledge` run-report to follow at Track time; working copy in the session scratchpad as `understand-map.md`.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY. The schema is a single embedded Rust constant `SCHEMA_SQL` (`crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/schema.rs:34-200`), every statement `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`, applied at exactly one site (`migrations.rs:92`). There is no ALTER TABLE anywhere in the workspace. The only versioning is `PRAGMA user_version`; `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1 (`schema.rs:27`) and `MIGRATIONS` is the empty slice (`migrations.rs:31`), with the forward-step machinery marked dead code — it has never executed in production or in any test. The defect is the early return at `migrations.rs:73-75`: a stale database is stamped 1, the constant is 1, so migrate returns success having run zero statements.

THE SHARPEST CONSTRAINT, and it is not the one the issue or the roadmap names. A stale database and a current one BOTH report `user_version = 1` — the stamp does not witness the column set, and `schema.rs:158-159` says so deliberately. So a step keyed on the version alone hard-errors with `duplicate column name: updated_at` on every database created since 2026-07-17, GA included. The fix proposed in this issue's own text ("schema_version bump + ALTER") does not clear that. The roadmap's stated constraint (do not add `dependencies.metadata` / `.thread_id`) is separately CONFIRMED — both are baseline columns present everywhere.

THE FULL SCOPE, settled definitively this session: the entire post-baseline schema delta is TWO nullable columns, `comments.updated_at` and `comments.redacted_at`, both added by commit c1cf5bb on 2026-07-17. `schema.rs` has four commits total; the other two change no non-doc line at all (verified per-commit, not inferred). No table, index, trigger or constraint was ever added, dropped or renamed after the baseline.

THE POPULATION IS NOT INTERNAL-ONLY — this closes the one check that would have permitted the cheap answer. Prereleases v1.0.0-rc.2 (published 2026-07-16 11:56 UTC) and v1.0.0-rc.3 (2026-07-16 14:56 UTC) are public, not drafts, and each shipped 21 installable assets. Both predate the comments commit. So a third party who installed either and initialised a workspace holds a database the GA binary cannot read. Declaring pre-GA databases unsupported can no longer rest on "nobody outside could have one".

BLAST RADIUS, reproduced live over the wire against a fabricated stale workspace. The failure reaches every hydrated read, not just the comment verbs, because the comment column projection is interpolated into the two issue-hydration queries. Failing: every `query` kind except count, `issue` show/create/create_bulk/update/close/reopen, all four `comment` actions, `claim`, `defer`, `diagnostics` stats and lint, and `sync export`. Three findings beyond the issue text: (1) `issue create`, `create_bulk`, `close`, `claim` and `defer` COMMIT and then report failure, because the engine re-reads and hydrates after the transaction — an agent retrying a "failed" create manufactures duplicates, demonstrated; (2) both health surfaces report green — `unblock migrate` says applied=false exit 0 and `unblock doctor` says healthy exit 0 on a database that cannot serve a read, and the integrity check is a page-level SQLite check that by construction cannot see an application-schema mismatch; (3) `sync export` is itself a casualty, so there is no in-product rescue — today the only recovery is raw sqlite3.

WHY THIS CLASS EXISTS AT ALL. No functional or non-functional requirement anywhere obliges a released binary to open a database written by an earlier one; the obligation lives only as prose inside two decision rows. The design spine declares the migrate method with an EMPTY doc comment and is silent on what a stamped version implies. The comments decision is the only v1-scope decision that never states its migration posture, while the three decisions around it each say explicitly that they carry no schema change. Every migration test covers either fresh-to-current or newer-than-build; nothing covers a stamp between them.

DECIDE phase complete (2026-08-03) — Miguel ruled all six forks the Understand map raised. Nothing was defaulted by the implementer.

1. MECHANISM. Keep the `PRAGMA user_version` ladder, bump the current version to 2, and write step 2 as an explicitly ONE-TIME shape-sensing reconcile: it inspects the `comments` table before acting, because today the stamp 1 covers two distinct physical shapes. From step 3 onward the invariant holds and is WRITTEN DOWN: a stamped version implies a known shape. The natural home for that sentence is the design spine's declaration of the migrate method, whose doc comment is currently empty — that emptiness is the root cause of the defect class, not just of this instance. The one-time exception must be documented loudly enough that no future step copies it.

2. REACH. Both physical shapes that have ever existed are migrated: the 5-column `comments` shape and the current 7-column one. This is bounded and enumerable — the entire post-baseline schema delta is two nullable columns in one commit, verified per-commit this session. It is also the only option that honours the roadmap bullet as written. The alternative (support GA and later only) lost its factual basis: prereleases v1.0.0-rc.2 and v1.0.0-rc.3 are public, non-draft, and shipped 21 installable assets each, both predating the comments commit — so third parties can hold the old shape. It was also not cheaper, since `sync export` is itself a casualty and that option would have had to fund a rescue path anyway.

3. FALSE-GREEN — RULED WIDER THAN THE RECOMMENDATION. The stale state becomes DETECTABLE and the error becomes ACTIONABLE. Today a database that cannot serve a single read yields an opaque `DATABASE_ERROR` with `retryable:false` and no hint, while `unblock migrate` reports applied=false exit 0 and `unblock doctor` reports healthy exit 0. Whoever meets this in the field gets told what happened and what to do. A general schema-conformance comparison inside `doctor` remains a separate, larger question (it touches the doctor-lite requirement's scope) — this decision is about not lying, not about building a conformance checker.

4. DECISION ID. This mints D46. Two independent triggers in the process guide point the same way: it is a separately-motivated decision (how the on-disk schema evolves for the product's life) AND it reverses a shipped clause ("NO migration, the current version stays 1, MIGRATIONS empty"), which requires reciprocal cross-references in both rows. Precedent is directly on point: D45 was minted precisely because a ruling reversed a shipped D44 clause. THE CASCADE IS LARGER THAN THE SPECIALISTS REPORTED and lands in ONE commit: the D-range bump at three doc sites (`CLAUDE.md:17`, the ci-cd doc's lint section, and BOTH halves of `xtask/src/doc_lint.rs:455` — the prose range AND the tokenizer alternation) PLUS two shipped required check scripts that pin the live range through their own knob (`scripts/checks/d44-create-deps-claims.sh:76` and `scripts/checks/ub-lp9.25-dangling-blocker-claims.sh:111`). Miss either script and two required jobs go red.

5. WHEN IT RUNS. Implicit on open for this step — two nullable column additions, no data rewrite, milliseconds — which is also the shipped model the migrate surface's own decision relies on. AND the policy is written down now: implicit only for additive/nullable steps; explicit for anything destructive, data-rewriting or long-running. The reason to name it now rather than later is that a shared-state migration in a future release will not be safe to run unattended inside an MCP server's startup.

6. CLASS GUARD. The fix carries a content pin on the schema constant, so that editing the DDL without either bumping the version or adding a step turns the BUILD RED. The defect's cause was that an in-place DDL edit was invisible to CI while the tree asserted in two separate places a rule that nothing enforced. This is the positive, spelling-independent form of the guard — the negative form ("did anyone edit the DDL?") is not writable as a check. The recurring cost is accepted deliberately: every legitimate schema change must re-bless the pin, which is the point.

NEXT: Spec/Plan, spec-first — the authoritative documents change before any code. Then the design Review gate, then Implement, then Verify.

SPEC/PLAN round two + DESIGN REVIEW GATE — verdict FAIL (2026-08-03). Second failed iteration on this artifact, so per the process guide's two-iteration rule this escalates to Miguel rather than looping again. Branch `ub-lp9.13-spec-r2`, commit 88e30c6, spec-only, 17 files. Three adversarial lenses plus a coordinator; the coordinator re-derived every finding from the worktree rather than aggregating.

WHAT ROUND TWO LANDED. All four must-fixes from the first gate did land: the interface spine's doctor and migrate command descriptions, the engine plan's doctor row, and the cli plan's doctor row including its test expectation. The new rulings landed too — the hint with its cost stated (the contract bump from the current published version to the next additive one, with the hash re-pin), the semver clause recording that the backward direction is not a break, and a new numbered non-functional requirement for on-disk backward compatibility. Checks actually run and green: the doc lint (19 docs, 6 classes), all three shipped check scripts, the formatter, and the xtask suite (130 tests).

THE FIRST BLOCKING DEFECT — a definition that is false of the code it names, and whose consequence is this very bug returning. The spec introduces a baseline-schema-version constant defined as "the version the embedded schema constant's tables correspond to" and assigns it 1 — while the same row states the embedded constant stands unchanged with all seven comment columns. A seven-column comments table is the version-2 shape. So the constant that names the embedded schema's version disagrees with the embedded schema. The consequence is concrete: the spec has the fresh path apply the embedded schema, stamp the baseline, then fall through the ladder, while every step from the third onward applies its statements unconditionally. The first future step whose column is ALSO added to the embedded constant therefore hard-errors with a duplicate-column failure on every fresh initialisation — precisely the failure this decision was minted to end. Two coherent disciplines exist for this and the spec asserts things true of neither exclusively. It is Miguel's call, and it is the escalation.

THE SECOND BLOCKING DEFECT — the hint cannot reach the user on the path the rulings made normative, and no crate is chartered to compose it. Verified independently in code: the migration runs implicitly on open through the config facade at `crates/unblock-config/src/context.rs:210`; the config error's coded-error implementation at `crates/unblock-config/src/error.rs:110-124` implements ONLY the code accessor and forwards nothing else; the trait default at `crates/unblock-error/src/coded.rs:32` returns no hint; and the cli boundary at `crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:115` builds the payload from that config error. So a hint attached at the storage layer is DISCARDED at the config boundary — while the published capabilities resource would advertise a contextual hint shape for that code, paid for with a contract bump. That is the ruling's own failure mode wearing the contract's clothes: advertise and discard, the same class this whole maintenance slot has been closing. The repair is mechanical once decided — widen the scope clause to include the config crate so it forwards the hint the way it already forwards the code, and name the crate and call site that COMPOSES the hint text, which today is specified only as "composed at the site" and names no file, type or method.

FINDINGS THE COORDINATOR KILLED, with reasons, rather than passing them along: the charge that pinning the guard's own survival in the check-script family is over-reach (the decision itself mandates it, precedented three times); that surfacing the never-existed function as plan-versus-code drift is over-reach (the process guide requires drift be surfaced); that the new requirement's reach exceeds the ruling (the ruling set a floor, not a ceiling, and the third database state is a real crash-window state the map flagged); an alleged spine-versus-crate-plan split (the spine is silent, not contradictory); and that the content pin misses the step's own statements (the ruling targets the schema constant, which the pin covers).

STILL OUTSTANDING FOR THE PULL REQUEST, not a defect: the run-report gate classifies this diff substantive on four independent arms, so the knowledge-layer run report and the tracker re-export must land in the same commit before the pull request can be opened.
